We address these challenges with Context-Aligned Turn-Level PPO, which uses a turn-level critic and computes policy updates using each turn's actual context. The resulting models, which we call AURA, substantially reduce all three weaknesses. Training improves the 8B model's score from 24.0 to 47.0 and the 30B model's from 27.4 to 54.7, with the latter surpassing all evaluated frontier models on our benchmark and achieving its largest margin on the most recent test period. These results suggest that agentic RL can improve performance on tasks with noisy, delayed real-world outcomes.

papers.title: Two families of Hermite normal form simplices
papers.abstract: We study Ehrhart coefficients, the integer decomposition property, and unimodular triangulations for two families of Hermite normal form simplices considered by Bruckamp, Caicedo, and Juhnke. The first family consists of simplices of the form $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}=\mathrm{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{d-1},\boldsymbol{a})$, where $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1},N)$, and the second consists of the simplices $T_{d,N}=\mathrm{conv}\bigl(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{d-2},(d-2,\ldots,d-2,d-1,0),(1,\ldots,1,N)\bigr)$. For the family $T_{d,N}$, we prove unimodality of the Ehrhart coefficients in every dimension and determine the log-concave and real-rooted cases. For the subfamily $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ with $\boldsymbol{a}=(N-q,\ldots,N-q,N)$, we characterize both the integer decomposition property and the existence of a regular unimodular triangulation via a congruence condition on a negative continued fraction. We also give an arithmetic test for the integer decomposition property and finite triangulation tests for $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ with arbitrary $\boldsymbol{a}$. These results address three open questions of Bruckamp, Caicedo, and Juhnke.

papers.title: ScAn-Bench: Evaluating Scaling Analysis Methodology
papers.abstract: Recent progress in machine learning is driven by large-scale foundation models, where scaling laws and finding optimal scaling prescriptions for architecture, data, and hyperparameters are key in advancing the state-of-the-art. Therefore, it is surprising that no systematic study evaluates the methodology to obtain scaling laws and prescriptions across different model types. To shed light on this crucial blind spot and facilitate future research, we introduce the surrogate benchmarks ScAn-Bench-LLM and ScAn-Bench-VLM based on 4524 and 8024 checkpoints of language and vision-language model pipelines. On our benchmarks, we perform the first systematic evaluation of both data acquisition and extrapolation methodology for scaling analysis across different data modalities.

papers.title: SkillPE: Creativity-Oriented Cinematic Skill Evolution for Text-to-Video Prompt Enhancement
papers.abstract: Achieving high-quality cinematic text-to-video generation remains challenging for non-experts, whose prompts often lack professional narrative and creative design. Existing prompt enhancement (PE) methods and static cinematic skills offer limited capabilities for exploring diverse creative realizations. We propose SkillPE, a creativity-oriented PE framework that systematically evolves reusable cinematic skills through reference-guided exploration. Starting from expert-provided cinematic knowledge, SkillPE initializes and normalizes 20 structured seed skills. It then retrieves movie references categorized as resonators (good matches), dissonants (weak matches), and divergents (creatively inspiring near-misses). Resonators and dissonants refine skill applicability and execution, while divergents inspire alternative cinematic realizations through controlled mutations that preserve user intent. Candidate skills are assessed through generated videos along prompt fidelity, cinematic quality, narrative appeal, and creativity to construct the final skill libraries. Experiments on StoryEval and VBench demonstrate improvements of up to 1.10 points over seed skills and 1.02 points over the strongest external baseline on a 7-point four-dimensional evaluation scale. Overall, SkillPE offers a practical approach to balancing fidelity and creativity in cinematic text-to-video generation.

papers.title: PhysAlign: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Role Alignment in Multimodal Physics Reasoning
papers.abstract: A key challenge in physics diagram understanding is correctly associating visual information with the physical entities, relations, and conditions it describes. Even when a value, symbol, or other local element is accurately recognized, assigning it to the wrong entity or scope can distort the underlying physical premise and lead to incorrect reasoning. To systematically study this challenge, we introduce \textbf{PhysAlign}, a benchmark designed to assess whether multimodal models correctly associate information recognized from physics diagrams with its intended physical role. By disentangling visual recognition from physical-role assignment through localized probes and controlled variants, PhysAlign isolates correspondence errors from recognition failures. It contains 3,341 human-validated probes spanning 986 physics problems, enabling systematic evaluation of visual recognition and physical-role correspondence at scale. We further introduce five complementary evaluation metrics, including CAcc, GAcc, and JAcc, which provide a comprehensive assessment of models' ability to recognize diagram content, establish correct physical correspondences, and solve the underlying physics problem. Across our evaluated multimodal models, PhysAlign reveals a consistent gap between local visual recognition and physical-role grounding. Even when the queried content is correctly recognized, the conditional correspondence error rate remains 13.8\% for GPT-6-Astra and rises to about 50.6\% for InternVL3.5-8B. These findings indicate that strong perception alone does not ensure reliable physical interpretation, exposing a distinct grounding bottleneck that is largely hidden by answer-level accuracy and highlighting the need for future models to better align recognized visual evidence with its physical meaning.

papers.title: Octree-based Video Representation
papers.abstract: Representing videos on uniform spatio-temporal grids produces large token sequences and substantial computational costs. Yet visual complexity is unevenly distributed: smooth regions can be represented compactly, while detailed regions require finer resolution. We introduce OctVideo, an octree-based video representation that adapts cell size to local approximation error. Each leaf stores local RGB values and spatio-temporal gradients, supporting analytic reconstruction of the video. A lightweight learned residual enriches these descriptors for neural processing. For reconstruction, a Conv1D VAE maps the serialized cells to a regular latent grid and selectively refines details during decoding. Our VAE achieves 36.12 dB PSNR with 38.2M parameters and 188.9 GFLOPs per clip on Kinetics-400 (K400). It also generalizes zero-shot to the high-resolution Densely Annotated VIdeo Segmentation (DAVIS) 2016 dataset with reconstruction quality comparable to the best evaluated models. On both datasets, it requires the fewest model FLOPs and achieves the fastest reconstruction among the evaluated models. OctVideo also supports video understanding, achieving competitive recognition performance with few input tokens when trained from scratch. By exploiting the redundancy already present in video signals and efficiently processing sparse structures, OctVideo provides an efficient representation for video.

papers.title: Intuition Vectors from Pretrained Representations Steer Diffusion-Based Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract visual reasoning requires identifying relationships between few examples and applying them to novel inputs. Recent advances have been driven by large language and vision-language models or specialized domain-specific architectures. It remains unclear whether abstract reasoning can be supported directly by the relational geometry of pretrained visual representations, without relying on language-based inference or task-specific representation learning. We investigate this possibility using frozen self-supervised vision encoders. With latent vector arithmetic, we confirmed that the representational geometry of two self-supervised encoders support abstract concept discrimination on Bongard problems and encode systematic relationships between input-output pairs in ARC tasks. Simple vector differences between image embeddings, which we call intuition vectors, capture transformations that generalize across instances of the same task. These vectors distinguish among 794 abstract reasoning tasks with up to 87.2\% accuracy, preserve relational structure across task-invariant visual transformations, and guide output retrieval for unseen inputs. Given this, we tested the hypothesis that this relational structure can steer generative reasoning by conditioning a diffusion transformer operating in pretrained visual latent space. On held-out ARC tasks, intuition-vector conditioning outperforms conditioning on complete demonstrations while requiring nearly six times less test-time compute, and supports zero-shot inference. Taken together, our findings suggest that pretrained visual representations provide a transferable substrate for abstract reasoning, enabling a modular approach in which the relational structure inferred from demonstrations steer generative reasoning.

papers.title: Rethinking the Reconstructio-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Fusing shallower encoder layers into a Representation Autoencoder (RAE) sharpens pixel reconstruction but degrades diffusion generation. Prior studies and the research community commonly attribute this trade-off to the latent content itself, assuming detail-rich features are harder to model. We show that this gap stems from geometric mismatch at the encoder-decoder interface. Freezing a foundation encoder preserves rich visual information, but imposes an encoder-native Euclidean metric shaped without pixel decoding, whereas the decoder amplifies sampling errors sharply along sensitive directions. At fixed information, reducing pixel error admits two dual geometric interventions: regularizing the decoder to flatten its sensitivity to latent variations, and aligning diffusion coordinates with the frozen decoder's metric at identical clean reconstruction. On ImageNet-256, aligning diffusion coordinates largely closes the guided generation penalty of multi-layer fusion and reaches state-of-the-art 0.984 gFID and 2.14 FDr6 in 80 epochs. RAEs should take information from the encoder and geometry from the decoder.

papers.title: Who Says What: Symbolic Trimodal Binding Mechanisms in Audio-Visual LLMs
papers.abstract: Current Audio-Visual LLMs (AVLLMs) struggle with reasoning over videos featuring multi-speaker dialogues. In such videos, resolving "who says what" is crucial, which necessitates trimodal (text-audio-visual) binding. Motivated by these challenges, we systematically investigate how this trimodal binding is achieved in AVLLMs. Specifically, we identify emergent symbolic trimodal binding mechanisms in AVLLMs that utilize modality-specific symbolic variables. By encoding auditory and visual components into symbolic variables-capturing temporal utterance sequences and spatial entity coordinates, respectively-the model establishes cross-modal linking within this abstract space. Crucially, we reveal that when trimodal binding fails, the breakdown predominantly stems from misaligned audio-visual connections. To overcome this bottleneck, we introduce an audio-visual prompting method utilizing an off-the-shelf Active Speaker Detection (ASD) model. By simply overlaying visual bounding boxes on active speakers, this training-free approach yields immediate performance gains across four conversation-centric benchmarks. Moreover, lightweight fine-tuning of fewer than 300 steps on these ASD-prompted-videos extends these gains to three general AV benchmarks, suggesting the generalizability of our method. Our code is available at https://github.com/kaistmm/Who-Says-What.

papers.title: Shielded Trajectory Sampling for Personalized Relational Safety in Conversational AI
papers.abstract: Anthropomorphic conversational systems can provide companionship and emotional support, but repeated, seemingly harmless interactions can encourage excessive dependence and reduced human contact. We formulate safety in user-AI relationships as a sequential decision problem, using conversational cues to track the relationship and selecting responses according to their anticipated effects over time. A conditional Generative Flow Network learns from sampled response plans to select replies that preserve the largest estimated mass of safe and useful continuations. Model-based checks screen plans during training and responses during interaction, requiring at least one sequence of future response strategies that meets a prescribed safety bound under every candidate user model, independently of the learned network. Strategies are selected directly from learned first-step probabilities, avoiding online plan sampling. We evaluate the approach in simulation against reactive safeguards, filters with and without memory, and alternative planners, using exact computation to validate the learned approximation. We also evaluate relational cue extraction from real user messages in WildChat. To our knowledge, this is the first approach to select conversational replies by anticipating their effects on the user-AI relationship while imposing an explicit model-based safety bound on future response sequences. Results show close agreement with exact planning, lower decision costs at longer horizons, and improved safety-utility trade-offs when protective responses are less effective. The approach balances immediate support with the longer-term effects of repeated interaction. The source code is available at https://github.com/benedettapicano/ANTHROPOMORPHIC_SAFETY_TRAJ.

papers.title: Periastron advance from the perturbed Binet equation
papers.abstract: We apply the Poincaré-Lindstedt method to the perturbed Binet equation describing conservative dynamics of the perturbed Kepler problem. We show that a simple treatment of divergent terms directly determines the frequency shift of the radial motion and hence the periastron advance. We provide explicit expressions for polynomial, logarithmic and inverse power perturbations, extend the procedure to higher perturbative orders and to problems involving several perturbation parameters. Applying this method to different physical effects relevant to compact binaries, we recover known results. We also obtain new contributions to the periastron advance, including the leading-order effects of arbitrary mass- and current-type tidal multipoles and mass-type spin-induced multipoles, the NNLO current-type tidal quadrupole contribution, electromagnetic electric-dipole contributions to NNLO and the eccentric corrections to the electric charge. Finally, we illustrate how the method can be directly applied to the problem of particle motion in Reissner-Nordström, de Sitter-Schwarzschild metrics and in a Yukawa potential.

papers.title: Quasi-symmetric error field correction and applications to ITER
papers.abstract: Reliable correction of nonaxisymmetric error fields (EFs) is essential to the safety and performance of tokamak operation. Although resonant error field correction (EFC) is well established, supported by an improved understanding of 3D plasma response, the residual fields left after resonant EFC remain an open question: they are expected to be predominantly nonresonant, yet can still degrade both confinement and stability. Here we introduce a systematic EFC scheme that minimizes resonant and nonresonant EF effects simultaneously, based on neoclassical torque response computed from self-consistent perturbed equilibria. The scheme extends the method developed for designing quasi-symmetric magnetic perturbations to the case where actual error fields are present. Application to standard ITER target plasmas with a range of intrinsic EF scenarios demonstrates the advantages of this quasi-symmetric (QS) EFC scheme for controlling residual EFs. QS EFC consistently yields low-torque solutions while strongly suppressing resonant response, outperforming single-mode resonant overlap EFC in most cases and approaching the performance of multimodal resonant EFC. We also show that the QS EFC solution varies only tolerably between half- and full-$I_p$ ITER scenarios, despite the greater sensitivity expected from its higher-order nature.

papers.title: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of superheavy $Z=124$ isotopes with the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum
papers.abstract: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of $Z = 124$ isotopes are systematically investigated using the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum (DRHBc) with the PC-PK1 density functional. By accounting for deformation and continuum effects, the neutron drip line is predicted to be located at $N = 320$, and eight potential multi-neutron emitters beyond the neutron drip line are identified. The results, compared with the spherically constrained case, highlight the critical role of deformation effects in determining the ground-state properties of superheavy nuclei. In addition, potential neutron shell closures emerge at $N = 258$ and $350$, alongside subshell closures at $N = 232$ and $320$. The results disfavor $Z = 124$ as a possible proton magic number and suggest $Z = 120$ and $138$ as more favorable candidates for proton shell closures in the superheavy region. Finally, the competition between $α$ decay, $β$ decay, and spontaneous fission is analyzed by calculating half-lives within various semi-empirical formulas. The results indicate that $α$ decay is the predominant mode on the proton-rich side, whereas spontaneous fission and $β^-$ decay gradually become dominant with increasing neutron number.

papers.title: Video-HopChain: Multi-Hop Questions and Confidence-Gated Exploration for Video Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: HopChain has shown on still images that multi-hop data synthesis improves vision-language reasoning, because long chain-of-thought reasoning exposes errors that compound across steps, while most data used for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) rarely demands a chain of visual evidence, so these weaknesses are likely to stay unexposed. We observe the same problem in video, where this framework has not yet been explored. We therefore build Video-HopChain, a dataset of 22,550 multi-hop video questions over 13,378 videos, together with a held-out benchmark of 1,000 questions. Each question chains three to six yes/no questions about moments in one video, and each yields one of two integers depending on its answer. The final answer is the sum of these integers, so an exact match on that sum gives the verifiable reward that RLVR needs. We first train Qwen3-VL-8B with GRPO on a standard video dataset, and a second stage on Video-HopChain then raises the mean over eight video understanding and reasoning benchmarks from 55.4 to 57.9 and improves every one of them. Training on such a dataset, however, exposes a known limitation of GRPO: its learning signal comes from the reward variance within a group, so hard questions whose rollouts are all incorrect and easy questions whose rollouts are all correct both leave the group with no gradient. To recover these groups at the same compute budget, we introduce Confidence-Gated Exploration (CGE). With 8 rollouts per question, CGE samples the first 4 as usual. If these 4 are either all correct or all incorrect, it samples the last 4 with the policy's most confident token masked inside the reasoning span, and removes the masked positions from the loss while all 8 rollouts enter the advantage. With CGE, the mean rises further to 59.3. We release the dataset, the checkpoint, and the data generation and training code.

papers.title: SPLASH: A Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy with Flash-Aware Sparse Attention for Long-Context Inference
papers.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash controllers that handle the access semantics and device management of flash. These controllers keep the GPU agnostic of the underlying memory, allowing the HBM-HBF hierarchy to behave as one logical memory for the KV cache. The added capacity of HBF enables long contexts, but dense attention, which reads the entire KV cache for every generated token, cannot keep decode interactive at these lengths. Splash therefore makes sparse attention flash-aware through query-driven address translation, in which the HBF base die resolves each query into the flash addresses of the relevant KV pages and schedules their reads across flash planes. Since the HBF base die holds the location of every page, this translation hides flash from the GPU and balances the selected reads across flash planes, coupling abstraction with performance. Across five models and up to one million tokens, Splash improves per-GPU decode throughput by up to 4.5x over the strongest baseline under a 100 ms latency budget.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations in two-photon-driven nonlinear quantum optical systems
papers.abstract: Understanding nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations under a parametric drive in nonlinear quantum optical systems is challenging. Here, we formulate a driven quantum master equation in the rotating frame combined with full counting statistics, retaining the drive-induced frequency shifts in the system-reservoir interactions and providing a unified description of drive-assisted incoherent transitions based on the rotated system dressed-basis. Applied to a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, the approach reveals pronounced multiphoton-resonant enhancement of the drive input energy current, with significant high peaks under two-photon driving compared to the single-photon case. The two-photon resonance relations are analytically obtained. Resonance structure in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model nonlinearly relies on qubit-photon couplings, with additional dressed-state branches. A low-energy-state approximation attributes the resonant current enhancement to dressed-state hybridization and efficient activation of incoherent energy exchange processes. Beyond the average current, two-photon-driving induced energy exchange picture near resonance also substantially modifies the second-order current fluctuation and higher-order current cumulant, while increasing the time-normalized signal-to-noise ratio. Adding two-photon loss introduces extra incoherent photon-pair exchange pathways and further reshapes the current and its fluctuations. We hope these results may deepen interpretation of photon driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively governing nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations.

papers.title: Prospects for testing Lorentz symmetry with highly charged ions
papers.abstract: We investigate the prospects for testing Lorentz symmetry using highly charged ions. We derive the Lorentz-violating energy shifts relevant to Zeeman and Zeeman-hyperfine transitions within the ground state of H-like ions and to Zeeman and Zeeman-fine transitions within the ground state of B-like ions. The resulting signals include sidereal variations through the first harmonic of the sidereal frequency for H-like ions and through the third harmonic for B-like ions. For certain SME coefficients whose contributions scale with the fourth power of the electron momentum, the large electron momentum in H-like ions can provide sensitivity competitive with the best existing bounds at the precision achievable in H-like-ion spectroscopy. We also find that B-like-ion spectroscopy can provide competitive sensitivity to certain SME coefficients.

papers.title: Uncovering Faithfulness Gaps in VLMs via Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can produce Natural Language Explanations (NLEs) that sound plausible yet remain inconsistent with the visual evidence they cite. We present Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing (EDCT), an intervention-based protocol that extracts visual concepts cited in a model's explanation, applies verified minimal edits to them, and tests whether the resulting answer and explanation remain consistent with the edited image. Using this protocol, we create EDCT-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark spanning three complementary domains: knowledge-intensive visual question answering (OK-VQA), safety-critical driving (DriveLM), and 3D spatial reasoning (3DSRBench). Across the evaluated VLMs, EDCT reveals substantial faithfulness gaps, with models frequently producing responses inconsistent with verified visual changes. Finally, our fine-tuning study suggests that EDCT-generated counterfactuals provide high-impact training signals.

papers.title: A General Inequality for Walks in Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and $w_k(G)$ denote the number of walks in $G$ of length $k$. For sequences $a_1, \cdots, a_n$ and $b_1, \cdots, b_n$ of non-negative integers such that $a_1 + \cdots + a_n = b_1 + \cdots + b_n$, we determine a simple necessary and sufficient condition on $a_1, \cdots, a_n, b_1, \cdots, b_n$ for the inequality \[ w_{a_1}(G) \cdots w_{a_n}(G) \geq w_{b_1}(G) \cdots w_{b_n}(G) \] to hold for any graph $G$.

papers.title: Control and Identification in Least-Squares Self-Tuning Regulation with Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: We study stability, minimum variance tracking and parameter identification for the Åstr{ö}m--Wittenmark self-tuning regulator with unknown input gain. Ordinary least squares (LS) estimates are used directly in certainty-equivalent control. Under the stated plant and martingale noise assumptions, we establish almost sure stability and optimal tracking for every bounded reference, provided that the gain estimates remain nonzero. When at least two parameters are estimated, all coefficient estimates are strongly consistent. The proof obtains a logarithmic information lower bound from an LS energy identity and uses it to establish gain consistency without assuming closed-loop stability. For at least two estimated parameters and every bounded reference, the squared error is almost surely $O(\log\log n/n)$ for the estimated ratios of the plant coefficients to the input gain and $O(\log\log\log n/\log n)$ for the full parameter estimate. A law of the iterated logarithm shows that the latter rate is sharp under zero reference. The bound for the full parameter estimate improves with reference energy, which also appears explicitly in the logarithm law for cumulative squared tracking residuals. These results show that optimal tracking can coexist with substantially slower estimation of the full parameter vector than of the coefficient ratios used in feedback. For at least two estimated parameters, a chi-square limit yields asymptotically exact confidence ellipsoids for every bounded reference.

papers.title: Current statistics for quantum transport along a bosonic tight-binding chain connected to Markovian reservoirs
papers.abstract: We study quantum transport of non-interacting particles in a bosonic tight-binding chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. Using the analytic solution in the form of an anti-normally ordered quantum characteristic function, we obtain exact probability distribution functions for the current on each bond in the chain, as well as the inter-bond current correlation functions. We extend the analysis to tight-binding chains subject to uniform on-site phase damping. In the phasedamped case, we find that a Gaussian approximation for the quantum characteristic functions predicts current fluctuations with good accuracy.

papers.title: Comparison-Based Fair Division of Indivisible Chores
papers.abstract: We investigate the query complexity of fairly allocating $m$ indivisible chores among $n$ agents with additive cost functions. We depart from the standard cardinal model and assume only comparison access: an algorithm is only allowed to ask an agent which of two bundles is less costly, and it never observes numerical costs. Our first results concern proportionality up to one item (PROP1). We design comparison-based algorithms that compute PROP1 allocations using $O(n^3\log m)$ comparison queries. When the chores are arranged in a fixed order, and allocations are required to be contiguous, we compute a contiguous PROP1 allocation using $O(n^5\log m)$ comparison queries. Our main result concerns the maximin share (MMS) guarantee. We show that for any fixed number of agents $n$ and constant $\varepsilon>0$, a $\left(13/11 +\varepsilon\right)$-MMS allocation can be computed with a comparison complexity logarithmic in $m$. Remarkably, comparison access suffices to match the state-of-the-art $13/11$ cardinal-access guarantee of Huang and Segal-Halevi up to an arbitrarily small loss. Furthermore, our result implies that the MMS distortion of comparison access (i.e., the worst-case multiplicative loss in MMS fairness incurred by observing only comparisons rather than numerical costs) is at most $13/11$. Finally, we show that, for three agents, an allocation satisfying envy-freeness up to one item (EF1) can be computed using $O(\log m)$ comparison queries.

papers.title: Reduction Modulo Binary Polynomials with Logarithmic Feedback Depth
papers.abstract: Polynomial modular reduction is central to binary finite-field arithmetic and repeated Frobenius powering. Top-down shift/XOR folding can use few operations when the nonleading support is sparse, but a tap near the leading term creates a long feedback chain. We formulate this recurrence as inversion of a nilpotent shift operator and factor its inverse by characteristic-two Frobenius powers. The resulting Frobenius-factorized reduction (FFR) applies to every monic binary modulus without materializing a reciprocal or dense reduction matrix, and its shifts can be generated online without a persistent modulus-specific schedule. For degree $m$ and nonempty nonleading support of size $s$, with nearest-tap distance $Δ_{\min}$, FFR uses exactly $\lceil\log_2(m/Δ_{\min})\rceil$ sequential feedback stages and has scheduled work $O(ms(1+\log(m/s)))$. A portable-C evaluation on 1,096 supports through degree $131072$ identifies distinct FFR, López--Dahab, and gf2x-backed Barrett regions. On four certified irreducible moduli, FFR makes complete Rabin irreducibility testing $1.35$--$8.04$ times faster than NTL and $1.60$--$6.81$ times faster than the matched Barrett implementation.

papers.title: Graph neural networks and the energetic cavity method for combinatorial optimization
papers.abstract: We study the use of graph neural networks (GNNs) for finding approximate ground states of Ising models. Efficiently finding these ground states is of broad significance because many combinatorial optimization problems can be formulated as an Ising model with the appropriate choice of couplings and fields. Exactly solving these problems is hard but there are many good heuristic methods. A lineage of these heuristics build from mean-field approximations: one approach uses the leading eigenvector of an appropriately defined matrix, another is the min-sum algorithm, also known as the energetic cavity method. Without modification, GNNs perform worse than both of these methods. We consider small modifications to the GNN to incorporate these heuristics and find that this considerably improves performance. While the modified approach is much stronger than other deep learning approaches, we still find that simulated annealing is generally as good for the same computational cost.

papers.title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Thermoacoustically Unstable Flames Via Non-Drifting Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: In this work, Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS) of thermoacoustically unstable free flames in closed-open tubes are presented. Simulations demonstrate nonlinear saturation of the primary instability as the flame flattens, resulting in a quasiperiodic acoustic limit cycle. Acoustic forcing is used to trigger secondary parametric instability, causing an oscillatory flame fingering characteristic of the unsteady Rayleigh-Taylor effect. To reduce computational cost, we perform DNS only on the region surrounding the flame. Acoustics at in- and outflows are described using the Navier-Stokes Characteristic Boundary Condition (NSCBC) method to model their delayed reentry into the domain in a formulation referred to as the Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Condition (ADCBC) method. A new Averaged Proportional and Integral Linear Relaxation (APILR) method is also introduced, which modifies the Classic Linear Relaxation (CLR) method to maintain time-averaged values of inflow velocity and outflow pressure. Many moving averages may be used consecutively to increase the damping rate of boundary reflection coefficients. An integral control term is used to remove non-zero equilibrium time-averaged inflow velocities which adversely affect control over flame position in the DNS region. Both new boundary methods demonstrate their capability in inert and counterflow flames test cases. In the case of a 100 cm long tube, these methods enable the numerical simulation of combustion instabilities at 98% reduced computational expense.

papers.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function is $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$
papers.abstract: We prove a weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal function with respect to Euclidean balls with dimensional dependence $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$. This improves the order of growth in the classical $O(n)$ estimate of Stein and Strömberg. The proof goes through a pointwise bound of the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator by the heat maximal operator with $\sqrt{n}$ loss. The key technical aspect of our result is an improvement of the weak-type bound for the heat maximal operator from $O(\sqrt{n})$ to $O(\log n)$.

papers.title: Amortizing Scaling Law Construction Costs
papers.abstract: Scaling laws guide the design choices for training large foundation models, but deriving them involves training an exhaustive grid over hyperparameters, token budgets, and parameter counts, which is computationally expensive. Fitting a scaling law, however, only requires the best-loss frontier across compute scales, discarding most of the trained configurations. We propose a framework for efficient scaling law construction that formulates data collection as a Bayesian optimization problem, and introduce metrics for comparing scaling law fitting methods under constrained compute budgets. We find that progressively expanding the compute budget during acquisition, mirroring the compute-ordered evaluation of configurations in practice, substantially improves recovery efficiency. Augmenting the observed configurations with surrogate-fantasized evaluations then recovers the broader experimental grid, allowing accurate scaling law fitting without training every configuration. Together, these can closely match scaling law fits over a full dense grid at computational savings of up to $10\text{--}100\times$.

papers.title: Optimisation of importance sampling implementation in rare-event shielding simulations using Geant4
papers.abstract: Rare-event search experiments demand ever-lower backgrounds, and the resulting radio-pure materials and suppressive shielding make related background simulations computationally expensive without event biasing. We present a method for optimising the widely used importance splitting and Russian roulette technique for rare-event searches, in which a whole number of equal-width importance layers fill the shielding geometry. Balancing relative uncertainty against execution time, we optimise the layer thickness for both $γ$-rays and neutrons, and across different shielding materials and thicknesses. Expressed as a multiple of the primary particle's mean free path, the optimal thickness generalises across energies for a given particle type and yields a physics-based prediction applicable to any shielding design. The same trend reveals that over-biasing is possible, with relative uncertainty worsening at high layer counts for fixed execution time. The optimal configuration gives an $\mathcal{O}$(20) gain in computational efficiency over the unbiased case.

papers.title: Homology of non-matching complexes under edge additions and applications to their Stanley-Reisner ideals
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph $G$ and an integer $t\geq 2$, we study the $t$-non-matching complex $\NM_t(G)$ and its Stanley-Reisner ideal. We prove that, if adding an edge $e$ to $G$ preserves bipartiteness, the inclusion $\NM_t(G)\hookrightarrow\NM_t(G+e)$ induces an injection on reduced homology in degree $2t-3$. If $G$ contains a cycle of length at least $2t$, then $\NM_t(G)$ has Leray number $2t-2$, and its Stanley-Reisner ideal has regularity $2t-1$. We also obtain explicit lower bounds for certain graded Betti numbers and the projective dimension of this ideal. If $G$ contains a $2t$-cycle, we determine the maximal shifts of this ideal through homological degree $|E(G)|-2t+1$. For the complete bipartite graph $G=K_{r, s}$ with $2\leq t\leq r\leq s$, we determine the depth, projective dimension, all maximal shifts, and the unique extremal Betti number of the associated ideal, thereby settling a conjecture on facet ideals of chessboard complexes.

papers.title: The role of different nonlinearities and potential vorticity conservation in two-dimensional fluid ITG models
papers.abstract: The nature of turbulent energy cascade of simple two-dimensional fluid models of ion temperature gradient driven turbulence is studied in detail. Notably, it is observed that a minimal two-field model of toroidal ITG behaves qualitatively differently with or without the diamagnetic nonlinearity. In its absence, the zonal flows always dominate and the system never reaches a high-transport state. In contrast, when this term is included, zonal flows dominate only near marginality, while away from it, an inverse cascade with high levels of transport is observed, requiring large-scale dissipation (hypoviscosity) to saturate and hyperviscosity to regularize small scale instability associated with this nonlinear term. However introducing such a term, together with the existence of the curvature term, breaks potential vorticity conservation, which is one of the key symmetries of drift-wave turbulence. This can be remedied by considering a more complete model that retains higher-order terms in the pressure equation. This form of the model, with four nonlinearities, conserves potential vorticity and behaves similarly to the original model, requiring hyperviscosity to saturate since the added nonlinearity generates small scale instability also for the pressure equation. To characterize the roles of potential vorticity conservation and higher-order terms in the pressure equation, the behavior of both the standard ITG system, and the potential vorticity conserving system, is studied by analyzing their spectra, turbulent cascades, and sensitivity to viscosity. Finally, the direction of turbulent cascade due to the different nonlinearities is investigated by examining their contributions to the spectral energy transfer and by considering the triadic instability assumption for each of these nonlinearities separately.

papers.title: Radiative pion-pair production in disperon QED
papers.abstract: Based on the previously developed disperon QED method for incorporating data input into loop processes in Monte Carlo codes, we calculate $ee\toππγ$ at NLO and include the pion vector form factor within the form-factor scalar QED approximation wherever it is physically justified. In particular, this includes insertions of the two-pion two-photon Compton tensor into loop diagrams. We also consider a subset of contributions beyond, involving the pion Compton tensor with three photons. For these terms the form-factor scalar QED approach is less well justified, but we gain insight into the associated theory uncertainty for selected experimental scenarios. All calculations are implemented and made available within the Monte Carlo framework McMule.

papers.title: The Safeguard Worked. Is the LLM System Safer?
papers.abstract: Safeguards for large language model services are typically evaluated by their attack-blocking rates on test suites. Deployment decisions also depend on how much harmful assistance attackers can still obtain from the system, which these rates do not measure. To determine what published evaluations establish about deployment safety, we develop a framework that translates reported results into the minimum and maximum harmful assistance that can remain under a specified outcome and threat model. For safeguards that block attacks through a check, we show that the most an attacker can obtain depends on three properties: whether attack paths pass through the check, its miss rate against every attacker in the threat model, and how much assistance remains after a block. We apply this framework to 85 safeguard evaluations from 52 papers. Of these, only five argue that every attack path passes through the check, and four provide evidence on what remains after a block. These evidence gaps have practical consequences: in NeMo Guardrails' default streaming configuration, the check blocked 94% of password leaks in our test, yet the client received the password in every leak, blocked or not. We identify which of the three properties each safeguard category's evaluations omit, and what to measure for each of four ways attacks bypass a check. Deployments that require these measurements before launch can choose and configure safeguards that limit what attackers obtain from the deployed system.

papers.title: Arabic Safety Alignment as Selective Refusal: An Empirical Study of SFT, DPO, and Guard Calibration
papers.abstract: Arabic large language models must refuse harmful prompts without over-refusing benign or sensitive prompts, yet a single refusal rate hides this trade-off. We evaluate it using benign refusal B and harmful-prompt refusal H, where H measures refusal rather than harmful compliance. Across five Arabic-capable models and 130 runs on the full human-written AraSafe set, refusal-only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) collapses toward blanket refusal, whereas selected mixed-SFT configurations reach H = 90% to 93% at B = 14% to 23%; four selected configurations exceed the H = 90% target in all three runs, while Fanar does so in two of three. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and inference guards change B and H differently across models rather than acting as uniform upgrades. In a blinded 300-response audit, annotator binary-refusal agreement is 89.0% (kappa = 0.78); Qwen3Guard and Aya Expanse 32B reach 88.7% and 91.0% accuracy, respectively, with no conclusive paired difference. Selected SFT raises H on Arabizi for all five models, but none reaches 90%, showing only partial transfer from Modern Standard Arabic. Overall, the results support model-specific operating-point selection: set a deployment target and retain only interventions that improve it.

papers.title: WALDO: One-Shot Exemplar-Conditioned Object Detection in Cluttered Scenes with World-Model Features
papers.abstract: Finding a particular object instance in a cluttered scene from a single reference image and saying when it is not there is typically given to large vision-language models. We ask whether the representations of a world model add something that the strongest self-supervised image features do not have. We introduce WALDO, a one-shot detector that finds a specific object instance in a cluttered real scene from a single reference image. Instance detection has usually needed per-object training. The alternative is a category-level open-vocabulary detector or vision-language model, which can find a mug but not this mug. We show that a lightweight conditioned head on frozen self-supervised features is enough to localize unseen instances without any per-object adaptation. We also find that image features and world-model features are complementary: DINOv3 and the video world model V-JEPA 2.1 succeed on different queries. There is one catch. Used the way video models are usually applied to still images, V-JEPA's dense features underperform. Reading them through the model's image pathway improves their localization. Combining the two backbones with a validation-tuned late fusion modestly improves DINOv3's localization of unseen instances without hurting its ability to tell whether the object is in the scene. A strong vision-language model and an image-guided open-vocabulary detector almost never localize the specific instance, and take far longer per query. Our fusion with world-model features strengthens localization from image features alone.

papers.title: Dandelion: A Spherical Flower for Neural Simulation of Planetary Dynamics
papers.abstract: Many dynamical processes unfold on the sphere but the default scientific machine learning architectures are Euclidean. Applying these architectures on a regular lat--lon grid causes problems: Cartesian convolutions become distorted at high latitude; 2D FFTs in Fourier neural operators incorrectly assume double periodicity; Cartesian positional encodings in ViTs distort spherical geodesic distances. Recent work moves towards natively spherical primitives, including spherical convolutions (e.g., DeepSphere or DISCO), Spherical Fourier Neural Operators (SFNOs), and geodesic attention. Here we propose Dandelion, a spherical version of Flower---a warp-based neural PDE solver. A Dandelion layer computes a tangent-plane displacement and then transports features along great circles. We obtain a U-Net-like structure by implementing hierarchical pooling entirely in the spherical-harmonic domain. There are thus no convolutions: spatial mixing is achieved only through spherical coordinate changes---or warps. To compare Dandelion with existing spherical architectures, we release an evolving benchmark suite of challenging, natively spherical PDE datasets including a modified Galewsky jet, anomalous chained turbulence, Cahn--Hilliard decomposition, spherical Riemann shocks, Held--Suarez dry atmospheric transport and global ocean dynamics. This new benchmark fills the gap between existing spherical datasets which are either too small and stylized, or much too large (ERA5) for model iteration. Dandelion achieves the best performance on all but one benchmark setting, where the best model is Flower2D, also based on warps. The spherical primitives result in the most physically consistent forecasts.

papers.title: Learning Complementary Routes for Scouting Persimmon Orchards during Shoot Growth with CoverShare
papers.abstract: At the study orchard, scouting during persimmon shoot growth focuses on leaf color change, leaf area, and internode length. Several routes may share an access lane, yet each can offer a view of row segments that the others miss. We introduce CoverShare to learn complementary routes under a fixed action budget. Within Policy Gradient for Parallel State Entropy maximization (PGPSE), CoverShare redistributes auxiliary rewards according to the state coverage lost when each policy is omitted and the number of policies visiting each state. It preserves the pooled entropy objective and total auxiliary reward. We simulated the annotated road network of a 6.7-ha site with 107 observable persimmon scouting units across five zones. At 40 actions per route, six distinct policies covered an expected 17.84 units perinspection, compared with 8.28 for six independent runs of one policy, averaged across eight training seeds. With the same policies trained on 40-action routes, extending each inspection route to 80 and 120 actions raised coverage to 22.52 and 28.38 units. Across seven public discrete-state tasks, CoverShare increased state support by a mean of 16.29% over the team-entropy baseline. Controlled ablations identified leave-one-policy-out coverage as the main contributor to these gains.

papers.title: Multi-Granularity Context-Enhanced RAG over Multimodal Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) leverages structured knowledge to provide large language models (LLMs) with high-quality external information. Building on these works, recent studies have explored multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) as knowledge bases for GraphRAG. This enables GraphRAG to integrate knowledge across multiple modalities, thereby further enhancing its performance. However, existing MMKG-based RAG methods generally follow a common pipeline in which different modalities are largely processed independently before being fused. As a result, textual context is only used to a limited extent during visual information extraction and subsequent multimodal knowledge fusion. This brings a semantic gap between images and text which limits the multimodal GraphRAG performance. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework for constructing a Context-Enhanced MMKG (CEMMKG) to better support multimodal GraphRAG. The proposed CEMMKG enriches each image with complementary textual context at both local and global scopes. Local context goes beyond the surrounding text by incorporating sentences that are semantically related to the image, while global context provides a summary of the entire document. We further introduce a multi-granularity design for the local context, allowing it to capture semantically relevant information at different levels of detail. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets validate that CEMMKG is effective in leveraging contextual information to improve MMKG-based RAG performance. Moreover, its effectiveness across different MMKG-based RAG methods demonstrates its broad applicability.

papers.title: Why ML-based cough models do not generalize: a systematic cross-dataset evaluation for tuberculosis screening
papers.abstract: Cough acoustics are promising for non-invasive tuberculosis (TB) screening, yet whether machine learning (ML) models capture disease-related acoustics or artifacts of data collection remains unresolved. We evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of classical ML and deep learning (DL) cough-based TB classifiers across three independent datasets. Despite moderate within-dataset performance (ROC-AUC up to $0.76 \pm 0.06$), both pipelines fail to generalize, with external performance frequently below 0.6, indicating a possible limitation of the data. We further observed that audio representations are organized by recording device and dataset rather than TB status, predicted TB probability tracks country-level prevalence in CODA, and device mismatch degrades transfer while device-diverse training improves it. Additionally, a clinical-variable baseline generalizes more consistently (ROC-AUC $0.65-0.71$), indicating acquisition-specific variability in acoustics is a stronger driver of poor generalizability. High within-dataset performance is not enough. External validation is essential before cough-based TB models are clinically ready.

papers.title: Fairness-Aware Test-Time Prompt Tuning
papers.abstract: Vision-language models have displayed remarkable capabilities in multi-modal understanding and are increasingly used in critical applications where economic and practical deployment constraints prohibit re-training or fine-tuning. However, these models can also exhibit systematic biases that disproportionately affect protected demographic groups and existing approaches to addressing these biases require extensive model retraining and access to demographic attributes. There is a clear need to develop test-time adaptation (TTA) approaches that improve the fairness characteristics of pretrained models under distributional shift. In this paper, we evaluate how episodic TTA affects fairness in CLIP classification under subpopulation shifts and develop FairTPT, a novel fairness-aware episodic TTA method that jointly minimizes target marginal entropy while maximizing spurious marginal entropy through soft-prompt tuning. We find that standard episodic TTA generally exacerbates disparities between majority and minority groups, that blinding a model to spurious attributes without degrading target performance is inherently challenging, and that excessive blinding can lead to catastrophic forgetting. This model collapse can be prevented by monitoring test-time changes in target loss within the linear regime, while still achieving fairness improvements on reactive data and preserving overall performance. FairTPT outperforms all state-of-the-art episodic test-time debiasing methods and establishes a foundation for robust TTA, which is essential for achieving fairness in practice.

papers.title: Spectral Geroch conjecture and noncompact area enlargeable summands
papers.abstract: We study complete metrics on area enlargeable manifolds through the spectral constant $Λ_γ(g)$, the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient of $-Δ+γ\mathrm{scal}_g$ over compactly supported functions. We prove that every complete metric on an area enlargeable $m$-manifold, $m\ge2$, satisfies $Λ_γ(g)\le0$ for all $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. For an area enlargeable manifold $M_1$ and an oriented manifold $M_2$ of the same dimension, we prove that $M_1\#M_2$ is area enlargeable if and only if $M_2$ admits a spin covering. Both summands may be noncompact. Consequently, if the universal covering of $M_2$ is spin, then $M_1\#M_2$ carries neither a complete metric of positive scalar curvature nor a complete metric with positive $γ$-spectral constant for $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. The threshold $(m-1)/(4m)$ is optimal. At the endpoint, the obstruction holds for metrics whose scalar curvature is bounded from below, but explicit complete warped metrics on $\mathbf{T}^{m-1}\times\mathbf{R}$ show that it fails in general. We also prove that the locally constant and the classical formulations of area enlargeability coincide in dimensions at least two.

papers.title: Wideband overlapped polyphase channelizer for kinetic inductance detector readout: split-path architecture and experimental characterization
papers.abstract: Frequency-multiplexed readout of kinetic inductance detector arrays measures the complex transmission of thousands of superconducting resonators. The channelizer that separates them introduces systematic effects: a gain that depends on where each tone falls in the channel grid, leakage between channels and added noise. This article presents a 4096-channel polyphase channelizer with 2/1 overlap for a 4.096 GS/s input, implemented on a first-generation radio-frequency system-on-chip, and a procedure to characterize it on the board with two receive chains, one digitizing the excitation as a reference. A split-path architecture computes the two overlap states in parallel filter branches at 256 MHz and reorders them frame by frame, under three control rules; it keeps only the transform stage at 512 MHz and affords a prototype of 16 taps per polyphase path (65536 coefficients) at the multiplication rate of a published 8-tap bank. Each selected channel is exported as a complex series at 1 MS/s. The measured channel response follows the coefficient-table model within 0.15 dB down to -28 dB, with both overlapping channels at full gain across their common band. Leakage into every measured channel 1.875 MHz or more from the tone is -94 dBc or lower, apart from images attributed to converter interleaving. The signal-to-noise ratio per sample lies within 1.7 dB of the limit set by the data-sheet noise density of the converter, and an emulated detector pulse is recovered with a decay time of 14.65 $μ$s (standard uncertainty 0.04 $μ$s), within 0.7% of the expected value.

papers.title: Cryogenic Mechanical Loss of GaAs/AlGaAs Crystalline Coatings
papers.abstract: Optical coatings with minimal thermal noise are essential for high-precision, laser-based metrology experiments. Substrate-transferred crystalline GaAs/Al$_{0.92}$Ga$_{0.08}$As coatings have the lowest thermal noise for high-reflectivity mirror coatings with $λ=900$ nm -- 12 $μ$m. Time-frequency stabilization experiments have demonstrated that GaAs/AlGaAs mirror coatings have a lower noise floor than amorphous mirror coatings. These mirrors are now being developed at sizes $\ge 300$ mm for gravitational-wave detectors. In order to understand the coating's fundamental loss mechanisms, which cause thermal noise, we have performed the first measurement of the mechanical loss at cryogenic temperatures using a cryogenic, multimodal, gentle nodal suspension system, which operates from 12 K to room temperature. This initial measurement used a silicon substrate whose asymmetry produced excess friction with the nodal support. Accounting for this friction and Akhiezer loss in the substrate and coating, the mechanical loss agrees well with the thermal noise observed in experiments using cryogenic fixed-cavities with GaAs/AlGaAs mirrors.

papers.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.

papers.title: When Candidate Pools Miss Active Constraints: Evidence from Electromagnetic and Thermal Design
papers.abstract: Finite candidate pools can limit surrogate-assisted design when good designs lie near intersecting active constraints. For independent uniform candidates in a normalized box, the typical minimum sum of gaps to k active bounds scales as (k!/N)^(1/k) for a pool of size N. This geometric limitation persists even with an accurate surrogate. We examine it through a controlled synthetic study and two finite-element design problems with inexpensive analytic constraints: a seven-variable electromagnetic coil and an independent six-variable heat spreader. The budget permits 25 initial observations and 50 further evaluations. On ten matched seeds, replacing pool EI with continuous constrained EI refinement raises mean coil response from 0.9120 to 0.9745 mT and lowers mean thermal resistance from 12.688 to 11.905 K/W. Standard continuous LogEI performs better than this refinement on nine coil seeds and all ten thermal seeds, reaching 0.9770 mT and 11.860 K/W. GP-mean search has the highest nominal coil mean but exhibits a thermal outlier on one seed. Mesh and domain checks preserve the substantial continuous-search advantage over the pool; they do not establish a resolved physical ranking among the closely performing continuous policies. Together, the sampling analysis and matched simulations identify when finite-pool search restricts the use of an FEM budget. The results support continuous constrained acquisition search, with stable LogEI as an effective existing implementation, when finite pools poorly represent high-value boundary designs. Bayesian optimization; acquisition optimization; active constraints; simulation-driven design; finite-element method; Gaussian-process surrogate; electromagnetic coil design; heat conduction

papers.title: PowerFull: fast and accurate computation of the relativistic angular galaxy power spectrum including local primordial non-Gaussianity
papers.abstract: Current and forthcoming wide-field galaxy surveys, such as SPHEREx and Euclid, provide a unique opportunity to probe the ultra-large scales of structure formation, where primordial non-Gaussianity, often parameterized by $f_\text{NL}$, is expected to leave its most detectable imprint. At the same time, these surveys inevitably enter regimes where relativistic and wide-angle effects become significant, requiring careful modeling to extract unbiased cosmological information. We address these challenges by applying the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation. The standard Fourier-mode description, which characterizes distortions by the angle between a mode and a line of sight, becomes ill-defined over wide fields, whereas the TAM basis naturally separates radial and angular contributions and incorporates the relevant relativistic effects. Within this framework, we provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions that can be compared directly with survey data. We then introduce PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, which enables efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Finally, using Fisher information matrix-based analyses, we show that a survey like SPHEREx reaches $σ(f_\text{NL}) \sim 1$, but that neglecting the relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered $f_\text{NL}$ by an amount of order its own uncertainty: at this precision the inferred value is biased unless the clustering is modeled consistently.

papers.title: When Detection Does Not Guarantee Resistance: Reasoning and Poisoned Context in RAG
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) exposes large language models to knowledge-poisoning attacks, where misinformation injected into retrieved documents can influence model outputs. Prior work has shown that models may detect contradictory evidence yet still allow it to influence their responses, revealing a gap between monitoring and control. We investigate whether deliberative reasoning changes this relationship. Because attack success and poison detection alone do not reveal whether detected poison continues to influence the final answer, we use two complementary measures: Cordon Rate, the probability that a model detects poison and nevertheless produces a poison-aligned answer, conditioned on a non-poison-aligned no-RAG response; and Leakage Rate, the probability that poisoned context influences the answer despite an explicit instruction to ignore retrieved documents. Across 200 SciFact questions, we compare reasoning-disabled and reasoning-enabled configurations of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.6-Plus. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, reasoning reduces Cordon Rate from 0.205 to 0.075 and Leakage Rate from 0.235 to 0.140, despite increasing Attack Success Rate from 0.233 to 0.298 and decreasing Poison Detection Rate from 0.965 to 0.665. Qwen3.6-Plus shows the same qualitative pattern. These results demonstrate that poison detection and downstream influence capture distinct aspects of poisoning behavior.

papers.title: Characterization of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule and lattice points in flagged hive polytopes
papers.abstract: We have previously, for a given positive integer $n$, explicitly characterized by certain linear inequalities the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux of shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ produced by $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson (LR) rule. We now extend that characterization for lower shape lengths. Then using the composition of promotion operators defining the Naito-Suzuki-Watanabe bijection between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux, we also explicitly characterize by certain linear inequalities the corresponding $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux when the shape length is $2n$ or $2n-1$. In addition, when the given $n$ is $3$ or $ 4$ the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and the $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux are characterized by linear inequalities for lower shape lengths. Since recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule are in natural bijection with Littlewood-Richardson-Sundaram (LRS) tableaux, we relate our results on the inverse quantum LR rule with other two bijections for the Naito-Sagaki conjecture and establish bijections between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux, $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux and the lattice points in a (disjoint) union of flagged hive polytopes.

papers.title: A Deployment-Oriented and Resource-Efficient Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Explainable DDoS Detection in Operational Technology Networks
papers.abstract: This paper presents a hybrid neural-symbolic detector of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on the availability of operational technology (OT) networks, designed for their resource-constrained gateways, and an evaluation matched to deployment. A compact gated recurrent unit (GRU) is fused at score level with a shallow, readable decision tree, and weight and threshold are selected on validation data under an explicit false-positive budget, whose attainment in finite samples is analysed. The evaluation on CIC-DDoS2019, Edge-IIoTset and CICIoT23 uses contiguous or capture-held-out partitions, dependence-aware intervals, and precision and alert load at operational prevalence. Over ten seeds at a 1% budget, the hybrid's false-negative rate on CIC-DDoS2019 is 0.08%, against 0.26% for the GRU and 0.17% for the tree. With a day of mostly unseen attack families held out, the tree alone carries the decision. Audits bound these claims: Edge-IIoTset is saturated by duplicates, no benchmark as used provides interleaved traffic in capture order, and an unconstrained tree is more accurate on two of them, so the case for the hybrid rests on short, stable rules and a measured footprint. On a Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 gateway, tested with Modbus/TCP and MQTT floods, the INT8 model needs 2.9 ms per window, 31 MB of memory and 3.5 mJ per inference.

papers.title: Three-body contact for fermions. II. Non-degenerate limit
papers.abstract: A fundamental quantity characterizing Fermi gases with zero-range interactions is the three-body contact $C_3$, which determines several observables including the number of nearby triplets of fermions and the three-body loss rate in cold atom experiments, as shown in a companion article. Here, we compute $C_3$ to leading order in the non-degenerate limit for the homogeneous gas with negative or infinite scattering length $a$. At $a=\infty$, using a wavefunction approach, we obtain the analytical expression of $C_3$, which has a remarkably slow $1/T^{0.22728}\ $ dependence on the temperature $T$. In the Feynman diagram technique, which we use for $a<0$, the correct three-body short-distance correlations emerge only after a non-trivial cancellation between leading order two-body and three-body correlations, and the resulting power-law scaling comes from the large-wavevector tail of the 3-body T-matrix, which we derive inspired by the analytical solution of the three-body problem at the unitary limit.

papers.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization on Reddit Was a Text-Length Artifact: A Reanalysis
papers.abstract: In the first version of this paper I reported that conservative Reddit users began writing more alike after ChatGPT was released while progressive users did not. That result came from a similarity measure that rises and falls with comment length. I redo every analysis of the original paper on all 6,056,593 comments with a sentence encoder and a dispersion measure computed within length strata, and the conservative break goes away. The two camps show no reliable difference in how within-group similarity changed after late 2022, and the ChatGPT date behaves like any of the more than two thousand other cutoffs I test. The matched flair comparison, the cumulative AI index, the stayer panel and the entropy signature each lose their support once length is held fixed. The one change that survives is older. Left and right comments drew closer to each other between 2019 and 2022, and that convergence was complete before ChatGPT arrived. I end with what this implies for studies that measure homogenization with embeddings.

papers.title: Modern aerodynamics models do not capture important unsteady forces and delays--the failure of the quasi-steady approximation
papers.abstract: Aerodynamic unsteadiness is inherent to the operation of many engineering applications, especially those that involve large-scale rotating blades, such as modern wind turbines. Over the past few decades, wind turbine rotors have grown rapidly and are now exceeding 200 meters in diameter, causing them to operate in conditions where limited empirical data are available, and where models have not been validated. Here, we use a highly pressurized wind tunnel to probe these conditions and evaluate the quasi-steady approximation, often used to simplify the modeling of the unsteady aerodynamic response of an airfoil to slow changes in inflow conditions. We find that the quasi-steady approximation is not valid for a large range of frequencies where it is normally applied. This finding suggests that the loading on wind turbine blades will be significantly underestimated when using conventional models, especially near stalling conditions, which modern wind turbines typically encounter.

papers.title: JWST detects a dusty AGB-like source before the Type Ia-CSM supernova 2026sqf
papers.abstract: Supernova (SN) 2026sqf recently appeared in the nearby face-on spiral galaxy NGC~3310 and has shown signs of strong interaction with a circumstellar medium (CSM). Such intense interaction, rare among nearby SNe, offers a valuable opportunity to reveal details on the origin and nature of its progenitor system. We analyzed the early-phase spectra and light curves (LCs) of SN 2026sqf. We identified a point source near the SN position in pre-explosion JWST and HST imaging, tested its association with the SN through astrometric alignment of pre- and post-explosion images and a chance-projection analysis, and constructed and modeled its spectral energy distribution (SED). The general characteristics of the spectra, the strengths of the emission lines, and the LC evolution all suggest that SN 2026sqf belongs to the rare SN Ia-CSM subclass, which would make it the closest known member (D~19 Mpc). The point source is a credible counterpart of the progenitor system, the first such identification for this SN subclass. Under our modeling assumptions, carbonaceous dust around a luminous evolved star provides a reasonable description of its combined SED; compared with local analogues, the candidate most closely resembles an extreme asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star. We report the first candidate pre-explosion counterpart of a thermonuclear SN identified in JWST imaging. Our results support the scenario in which SNe Ia-CSM emerge from a system consisting of a white dwarf and an evolved giant (probably AGB) star. Strong binary interaction, possibly involving common-envelope evolution or a merger, is a natural explanation for the observed properties of the SN and its candidate counterpart, though the channel and timescale remain uncertain. Late-time follow-up, especially with JWST, will test the identification and the conclusions of our early-phase analysis.

papers.title: Semantic Prism: Generative Segmentation with an Explicit Semantic-Image Interface
papers.abstract: Conditional image generators can render segmentation maps as semantic RGB images, but color drift and boundary mixing can undermine direct decoding. We present Semantic Prism, a framework that combines an explicit semantic-image interface with hierarchical refinement for road-scene segmentation. A generator adapted from a diffusion-distilled backbone produces a semantic RGB image with a single denoising update per crop. Distances to a fixed class-color codebook define interface logits and pixelwise class probabilities. Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment (HGEA) combines spatially aligned multilevel features from the VAE encoder of the generator with the input image, generated semantic image, and interface probabilities to predict additive corrections to these logits. Contextual Interface Hierarchy Disagreement (C-IHD) combines pointwise uncertainty, local context, and interface-refinement disagreement in a fixed score for ranking pixel errors, without an auxiliary predictor or an additional network pass. On the 500-image Cityscapes validation set, Semantic Prism achieves 72.07% mean mIoU, improving on direct-interface decoding by 11.39 percentage points. Extensive capacity-matched ablations show higher mean mIoU for multilevel refinement than for flat and single-level alternatives. The Cityscapes-trained model transfers to ACDC Dataset, achieving 46.89% mIoU without target-domain adaptation. Beyond Cityscapes, on BDD100K dataset, a separately trained model achieves 62.22% mIoU on its full 1,000-image validation set. Across the 3 evaluated datasets, C-IHD improves pixel-error area under the AUPR over uncertainty derived from maximum softmax probability, with segmentation predictions held fixed for each comparison. In particular, on ACDC, AUPR increases from 0.6580 to 0.7557, demonstrating that Semantic Prism presents more effective error ranking under adverse-condition domain shift.

papers.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: A Benchmark for VLM Readiness in Safety-Critical Scenarios
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are often deployed as embodied controllers for robotics, yet it remains unclear how well they can explore an environment, maintain an internal map, and ground safety-critical decisions in long-horizon sequential trajectories. In this work, we introduce EMRD, an evaluation framework that decouples spatial reasoning into four stages: Explore (what the agent observes), Map (what it records and where), Remember (what it retains), and Decide (whether its final choice is justified), scored across 18 stage-specific metrics. We use EMRD to evaluate eleven open- and closed-weight VLMs across 16 buildings under nominal conditions and three environmental stresses (darkness, smoke, and motion noise), where an embodied VLM explores unknown rooms, maps observed objects, and selects the safest gathering place. Open-weight models leave rooms unvisited in 95% of episodes and detect at most 51% of objects; closed-weight models explore more, though with an external memory (notepad), two of the three stop prematurely. Without external memory, most VLMs keep fewer of the objects they saw, especially in larger buildings. The start limits which rooms are explored, and open-weight models started in different rooms agree on the final room not significantly more often than chance. Moreover, these choices are biased by semantic priors: swapping a room's label is often enough to change the final choice. Finally, motion noise increases object position error (by 12-60% for closed-weight models), strong darkness lowers map recall by 28-31 percentage points, and dense smoke reduces seen objects by 25-39 points, while the choice among the rooms entered does not change significantly.

papers.title: MAGIC-SSCIL: Manifold Anchoring and Geometric Incremental Calibration for Semi-Supervised Class Incremental Learning
papers.abstract: Exemplar-free semi-supervised class-incremental learning (SSCIL) asks a model to learn new classes from a few labeled and many unlabeled images without storing past data. A common recipe replays old classes from stored Gaussian statistics and pseudo-labels unlabeled data with a confidence threshold. With one or two labels per class, however, the model's confidence is a poor guide to which pseudo-labels are right, so the statistics that replay depends on rest on few or noisy samples. We propose MAGIC (Manifold Anchoring and Geometric Incremental Calibration), which propagates labels over a k-nearest-neighbor graph of frozen features and uses the propagated confidences as weights in the unlabeled loss and, through Soft-Weighted Geometry Calibration (SWGC), in the class statistics from which phantom features replay old classes. With a frozen ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R at 1%, 5%, and 10% labels, we compare MAGIC with nine supervised class-incremental methods equipped with FixMatch and two native SSCIL methods. MAGIC gains from unlabeled data in all nine settings, most at 1%, and leads on fine-grained CUB-200 at every ratio; at 1% it is level with the best on ImageNet-R and 2.2 points behind the native SSCIL method TACLE on CIFAR-100. Experiments inside MAGIC show that most of this gain flows through the weighted statistics, not the loss, that at 1% labels graph pseudo-labels are more accurate than the model's own at equal coverage, and that a fixed threshold of 0.95 removes most of the gain. At higher ratios, baselines that adapt the backbone or model full covariances overtake MAGIC on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-R.

papers.title: Observation of far-from-equilibrium scaling in the transient dynamics of 2D quantum magnets
papers.abstract: The transient regime of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics lacks the established organizing principles that universality and scaling provide in equilibrium. It is least understood for two-dimensional short-range interacting systems, where mean-field arguments are not expected to hold, controlled theoretical descriptions are few, and fluctuations are strong. Here we investigate the quench dynamics of the transverse-field Ising model using programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realizing honeycomb, square, kagome, and triangular lattices. Starting from a fully magnetized state, we observe a pronounced softening of the dominant collective magnetization oscillation accompanied by a maximum in the damping rate, signaling a crossover between interaction- and field-dominated transient dynamics. Even though the microscopic lattice geometries are different, both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates collapse onto common curves under rescaling by the coordination-number-weighted interaction strength. We present a theoretical description which accounts for the collapse of both quantities and elucidates the nature of the processes responsible for the damping. The observed failure of the discrete truncated Wigner approximation to predict the damping for strong interactions shows that classical evolution of initial quantum noise is insufficient, while tree-tensor-network simulations reproduce the dynamics accurately.
