papers.title: On the equivalence of three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff models to the classical CBS equation
papers.abstract: We examine the three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff (CBS) models introduced by Wazwaz, Alhejaili, and El-Tantawy [Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ Plus \textbf{141}, 1218 (2026)]. Explicit invertible point transformations map the first model, and generically the second, to the classical CBS equation. The third model is generically equivalent to CBS with an additional spectator coordinate absent from the differential operator. We identify the exceptional parameter regimes and explain the reported exponential dispersion relations through these transformations. These equivalences show that the proposed models do not, in the generic parameter regimes, introduce new point-inequivalent CBS equations or genuine four-variable differential coupling.

papers.title: Non-tempered GGP conjecture for classical groups: the Bessel case
papers.abstract: In their recent paper, Gan, Gross and Prasad proposed a precise conjecture to describe the restrictions of representations of classical groups that lie in an L-packet of Arthur type. On top of local root numbers, the main notion considered is the relevance of two A-parameters. In this paper, we establish that the relevance of two A-parameters is sufficient for the existence of a Bessel period for a pair of representations in the associated L-packets. Moreover, such a pair is unique. We also prove the necessity of relevance for co-tempered A-parameters, and give several counterexamples in the general case.

papers.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
papers.abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenance. The wafer lot size, arrival profile, and factory maintenance policy are used as static covariates. TCNA is applied to a selected set of simulated discrete-event throughput and turnaround time trajectories. The $TH$ and $TA$ time series predicted by TCNA, evaluated with the common $MAPE$, $MSE$, and $R^2$ measures, show comparable or higher accuracy relative to other model architectures, with similar parameter counts and epoch times; the TCNA model size and execution time are similar to those of other architectures such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer. Although time series predictions are less accurate than high-resolution simulations, they can be deployed at a much lower computational cost. The TCNA achieves orders-of-magnitude speedup over PDEVS simulation with an acceptable loss of accuracy, enabling frequent product scheduling, capacity planning, and maintenance planning.

papers.title: Weighted Sum-Rate Optimization of Near-Field STAR-RIS-Aided ISAC Systems Under Hardware Impairments
papers.abstract: This paper investigates weighted sum-rate (WSR) optimization for a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS)-assisted multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system operating under the energy splitting (ES) protocol. A hybrid propagation model is considered, where the base station (BS)-STAR-RIS channel follows far-field propagation, whereas the STAR-RIS-user channels are modeled using near-field spherical wavefronts. Practical hardware impairments (HWIs), including STAR-RIS phase perturbations and signal-dependent additive distortion at the BS and user equipment (UEs), are incorporated into the system model. Under this framework, the WSR maximization problem is formulated subject to radar beampattern, quality-of-service, transmit-power, and STAR-RIS ES constraints. The resulting problem is highly non-convex due to the coupling among the active beamformers, passive STAR-RIS coefficients, and HWI-dependent signal-to interference-plus-noise ratio expressions. An alternating optimization (AO)-based successive convex approximation framework is developed to iteratively solve the active and passive beamforming subproblems. Numerical results demonstrate stable convergence of the proposed algorithm and consistent WSR improvement over direct-link transmission. Besides, severe HWIs also lead to WSR saturation in the high transmit-power regime, whereas stringent sensing constraints reduce communication throughput. Increasing the STAR-RIS aperture and the number of BS antennas improves the achievable WSR, although the performance gain becomes limited under strong hardware distortion.

papers.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $Γ$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. We further show that external vertical electric fields, twist engineering, and both out-of-plane and in-plane strain provide efficient means to tune the band alignment, charge transfer, and Rashba parameters. In particular, electric fields and mechanical strain can drive reversible transitions between type-II and type-III band alignments while simultaneously modifying the Rashba spin texture and the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) window. The twisted heterostructure with $θ= 21.79^\circ$ exhibits similar tunability, including strain-induced transitions between distinct band-alignment regimes. These findings establish MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs as versatile multifunctional platforms combining electrically tunable Rashba spin splitting with controllable type-II/type-III band alignment, offering promising opportunities for next-generation TFETs and spintronic devices.

papers.title: False Discovery Rate Control in Ordered Sequential Testing: Rejection-Count and Fallback Procedures
papers.abstract: We study false discovery rate (FDR) control for a fixed family of hypotheses tested sequentially in a prespecified order. Each decision uses only the current and preceding $p$-values, is not subsequently revised, and permits continued testing after non-rejections. We distinguish generalized fixed-sequence procedures based on preceding rejection counts from fallback-type procedures that additionally use recursively transferred testing levels. For rejection-count procedures, we study a position-dependent calibration under independence and a linear rule calibrated through null marginal distribution functions under positive left-tail dependence under the null. We clarify their connections to existing fixed-sequence and online FDR methods. The fallback construction combines the total number of preceding discoveries with level transfer along consecutive rejections, allowing thresholds to reflect the arrangement of earlier outcomes. We establish its FDR control under history-based positive regression dependence and, with a position-specific correction, under arbitrary dependence. For all four constructions, the guarantees extend to every deterministic testing time within the planned horizon. Gaussian simulations assess the effects of signal placement, dependence, and allocation weights. They demonstrate power gains over selected benchmarks while identifying the conservativeness of the arbitrary-dependence correction.

papers.title: Time-Varying Coverage via Diffeomorphic Coverage Control
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a structured class of time-varying coverage control in which region-density evolution is parameterised by a time-varying diffeomorphism acting on a static region-density pair. We refer to this setting as diffeomorphic coverage control. Such trajectories arise naturally in mass-conserving transport flows and in density-driven formation control. We propose decentralised diffeomorphic coverage controllers for both continuous- and discrete-time dynamics that achieve time-varying coverage by solving a related time-invariant coverage problem in a nominal domain. The resulting controllers are asymptotically stable with respect to a variant of a popular coverage metric under corresponding time-varying regions and densities. Further analysis shows that diffeomorphic coverage corresponds to a time-varying non-uniform coverage problem over a non-Euclidean metric. Simulations demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed control strategy under affine diffeomorphisms in a formation control task, achieving performance comparable to a popular centralised coverage control law. Coverage performance is also demonstrated under non-affine diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
papers.abstract: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.

papers.title: Target Detection with Tightly-coupled Wideband Antenna Arrays
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on tightly coupled antenna (TCA) array systems with high mutual coupling, resulting in wideband signals. We analyze the target detection capability of such systems with joint time and frequency approaches. We assume a target whose echo signals are unknown wideband signals and show the opportunity that TCAs create in target detection. We consider temporal and spectral dynamics of the signal as either constant, slowly or rapidly varying in frequency and time, giving nine possible cases in total. For each case we derive a detector and present thorough analysis for the distribution of the detector test statistic, considering frequency-dependent noise correlation due to mutual coupling. For the cases with a signal changing slowly in at least one domain we propose a novel detection approach based on estimation of the signal via local averaging of the samples. We also derive a detector that results in an upper bound on detection performance for comparison. We compare our analytical results with simulations, showing perfect accuracy of our derived distributions. In addition, we assess the performance of the detectors under various time/frequency variation rates. We show the superior performance of our proposed detection approach in comparison to other detectors including an extended energy detector we derive for correlated noise as well as both frequency and time samples.

papers.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
papers.abstract: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

papers.title: PromptPoseFX: Authoring Pose-Driven Visual Effects through Augmented Prompting and Interactive Refinement
papers.abstract: Human pose-driven visual effects offer a compelling way for enhancing video expressiveness and storytelling. Authoring such effects with traditional video editing tools is a complex and time-consuming task that requires considerable technical expertise and manual effort. While generative AI models can simplify the workflow by reducing manual scripting through language-driven generation, existing approaches suffer from imprecise alignment between visual effects and pose data, failure to preserve original video content, and limited support for fine-grained, iterative refinement. To address these challenges, we present PromptPoseFX, an interactive system that allows creators to author pose-driven visual effects through augmented language prompts and interactive refinement. Our system leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to translate high-level user intent into parameterized procedural graphics scripts, automatically mapping pose-tracking data to specific effect parameters, allowing precise alignment with human motion. This script-based approach manages effects as independent layers, thereby preserving the original content of the underlying video. To reduce language ambiguity, our interface offers controls across spatial, temporal, and parameter domains, enabling the precise, intuitive, and iterative authoring of pose-driven visual effects. We evaluated PromptPoseFX through a comparative study against a text-only LLM interface, followed by an exploratory study. In the comparative study, participants rated PromptPoseFX significantly higher than the text-only baseline on measures of perceived control and precision. The exploratory study examined usability and creativity support in open-ended authoring tasks.

papers.title: Agent-Guided Configuration Tuning for SMT Solvers
papers.abstract: SMT solvers expose many configuration choices that determine how well their existing algorithms perform on a workload. We present, to our knowledge, the first workflow that uses general-purpose LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations. Agents read solver documentation, source code, and persistent experiment records to propose option changes, and a deterministic harness measures each proposal, validates the returned models, and selects changes separately for each competition Division. Over roughly nine weeks, our tuning campaign recorded 4,545 proposals for cvc5 across 13 Divisions and 36 logics. We evaluate the tuned configurations on the 2026 and 2025 SMT-COMP ModelValidation benchmarks under a 24-second cutoff. On problems not used for training, they validate more problems than official cvc5 in ten of the 13 Divisions in 2026 and in eight in 2025, with geometric-mean gains of 7.8% and 6.8% across Divisions. On the complete official selections, which include training problems, the tuned floating-point counts exceed those of every individual competition participant in both years. Further studies show how configuration changes make existing algorithms effective by changing access to strategies, scheduling, and option compatibility, and how benchmark families trade off against one another. The agents' experiment traces contain hypothesis-based proposals in every tuning group, and 64.3% of the extracted hypotheses draw on prior measurements. These results show that agent-guided tuning can specialize a mature SMT solver and that accumulated experimental evidence informs sustained search.

papers.title: Parallelizable Interior-Point ADMM for Block-Structured Nonconvex Programs
papers.abstract: Physics simulation is an increasingly important computational primitive for AI, and local--global/ADMM splitting exposes its parallel structure but lacks matching finite-time convergence guarantees. We close this gap with two ADMM variants, Interior-Point ADMM (IP-ADMM), for block-structured nonconvex composite programs with smooth nonlinear inequality and affine constraints. A one-sided finite-activation wall keeps each constraint split state strictly feasible while the original-space infeasibility vanishes, giving closed-form constraint updates, one proximal call per objective block, and one equality-constrained quadratic consensus solve per iteration. \rev{To our knowledge, this makes IP-ADMM the first single-loop method that updates nonconvex inequality constraints locally and in parallel with finite-time convergence guarantees.} Ordinary IP-ADMM attains a CQ-free best-iterate weak-KKT rate of $O(K^{-1/3})$ or a banded Fritz--John rate of $O(K^{-1/4})$, which converts to KKT at $O(K^{-1/4})$ under a uniform constraint qualification; these are nearby-point certificates that reduce to conventional KKT for smooth blocks. A checkpoint variant, IP-ADMM-Ckpt, improves the asymptotic KKT exponent to $O(K^{-1/3})$. We also show how the bounds scale with the objective- and constraint-block counts and the coupling norm.

papers.title: General Formulation of Covariant Tensor Amplitudes for Purely Hadronic and Single-photon Radiative Cascade Decays
papers.abstract: We present a unified method for generating Lorentz-covariant partial-wave amplitudes for multi-body purely hadronic and single-photon radiative cascade decays within the covariant $L$-$S$ tensor formalism. Based on the structural decoupling of external polarization wave functions, complex coupling parameters, and the core covariant amplitude tensor $U$, we establish a hierarchical vertex contraction procedure that explicitly incorporates intermediate-state cascade bridge projection operators $P^{(J_i)}(p_i)$ and parent-frame definite-spin projection operators $P^{(S_{BC})}(p_A)$. This rigorous treatment guarantees the Rarita-Schwinger symmetry, tracelessness, and transversality conditions across different reference frames, fundamentally eliminating the unphysical longitudinal and trace contaminations induced by Lorentz boosts in cascade decays. Furthermore, we formulate a general covariant tensor representation for single-photon radiative decays $A(J_M) \to γ+ X(J_X)$ that strictly satisfies photon gauge invariance ($q^λV_{\dotsλ\dots} = 0$) in the Lorenz gauge. Built upon normal- and anomalous-parity fundamental transverse tensors ($K_{μν}$ and $S_{μν}$), universal recursive formulas are derived via the systematic replacement $g_{μν} \to q_μp_{Aν}$, accompanied by exact rules for matching the orbital angular momentum ranks of Blatt-Weisskopf centrifugal barrier factors $B_{L_{\text{rad}}}$ and a spectator index pass-through mechanism for the photon polarization index.

papers.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense 3D representations by adaptively aligning features in the policy's shallow layers with the intermediate representations extracted from multiple 3D FMs. Building upon these lifted representations, the See phase equips the policy with explicit geometric and interactive awareness through dual guidance. It introduces depth-map reconstruction to help the model comprehend 3D spatial layouts and utilizes hand region cues to explicitly supervise the encoder's attention toward task-relevant interaction hotspots. Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, our policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase. Extensive experiments on diverse simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that LSA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches. The project page is available at: https://yiyuan00.github.io/Lift-See-Act.

papers.title: Separating learning from search and feedback in budgeted inverse design of periodic unit cells
papers.abstract: To design a periodic material, engineers choose the shape and dimensions of a repeating cell to meet target properties. With few simulations, the benefit of a learned predictor can be hard to separate from the effect of which designs the search tries and how it uses simulator feedback. We compare two ways to predict properties in a library of 80 cell architectures, with up to 30 simulator calls per target. For each architecture, both searches use a table of predicted properties at different dimensions. One fills the table with predictions from neural networks. The other fits a simple model to the existing simulations for that architecture. Both searches use the difference between the predicted and simulated properties to adjust the next design. We generated 200 targets from simulated designs after fixing the analysis plan. The two searches showed no detectable difference in how often they matched all three properties within 2% or in the mean error of their returned designs. The upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the gain in overall success rate was 4.5 percentage points. Follow-up controls on these targets changed success from 83.5% to 36.0% with a degraded table and 96.5% with an oracle table. In separate tests, using the simulation result to adjust the next design increased success for both types of table. Results cover one library and a coarse 32^3 voxel simulator. Designers can use this comparison to judge what a learned predictor adds when the search, feedback and budget are the same.

papers.title: Broadband Absorption Bounds for Coated PEC Spheres: Curvature, Angular Momentum, and Localized Sources
papers.abstract: We investigate fundamental limits on broadband electromagnetic absorption by a material-coated perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere. Exact reflection coefficients are derived for the transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) spherical modes. Their long-wavelength asymptotics, combined with causality and contour integration in the complex wavelength plane, yield sum rules relating the wavelength-integrated modal reflection to the static material parameters, coating thickness, curvature, and complex reflection zeros. For the dipolar modes ($n=1$), known passive spherical-wave sum rules establish analytically a material-dependent lower bound on the weighted logarithmic reflection integral. Extension to higher-order modes requires a nonnegativity condition on higher odd moments of the reflection zeros; we formulate this condition as a conjecture and provide extensive Monte-Carlo evidence for passive dispersive coatings. The resulting bounds establish a per-channel absorption--bandwidth tradeoff and reveal the spherical-harmonic order as a discrete transverse-wavenumber variable, recovering the familiar planar attenuation factor in the locally planar limit. Finally, we show how the modal bounds can be combined for a localized external source. For a radial electric dipole outside the sphere, the near-field excitation is decomposed into TM spherical channels, leading to a source-weighted broadband absorption bound. As the source approaches the surface, progressively higher angular momenta contribute, directly linking near-field spatial localization to the hierarchy of modal absorption constraints.

papers.title: Beyond Seeing: Fine-Grained Preference Validation and Severity-Aware Alignment for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models can produce fluent responses containing objects, attributes, or relations unsupported by the image. We study an implemented alignment pipeline that normalizes released fine-grained hallucination supervision, validates chosen-rejected preference pairs with vision-language judges, repairs rejected chosen responses, and trains LLaVA adapters with standard or severity-aware direct preference optimization. The study uses 16,143 normalized feedback records and 8,386 released preference pairs, comparing direct training with zero-shot and two-shot judged severity-margin variants. The zero-shot variant reduces Object HalBench CHAIRs from 53.00 to 36.00 and CHAIRi from 15.72 to 10.41. Across aligned models, AMBER-Hal decreases from 35.90 to 25.10-26.90, accompanied by reduced visual coverage. In contrast, the base model retains the highest valid POPE adversarial F1, 84.18 versus 83.87-83.91 after alignment. These results support benchmark-dependent reductions in generative hallucination rather than uniform superiority of severity-aware alignment. We distinguish implemented pipeline components from the preference paths used in the reported experiments and discuss the limits of attributing gains to judging, repair, or the training objective individually.

papers.title: Tangent lengths and invariants of Poncelet polygons between two circles
papers.abstract: A polygon inscribed in one circle and circumscribed about another moves in a one-parameter family, by Poncelet's porism. We study this family through the tangent lengths from the vertices to the inner circle and find a number of quantities that remain constant during the motion. For example, the sum of the fourth powers of the distances from the circumcenter to the points of contact, plus twice the squared area, is constant. We also obtain a version of Euler's formula for $n$-gons, extend a problem on bicentric hexagons from Kvant, and find a second quadratic invariant that goes along with the classical theorem of Weill. The basic invariants have elementary proofs; for the main ones we give two proofs, one of them without derivatives. Reciprocation at a limiting point of the two circles turns these results into statements about billiards in ellipses, and gives short proofs of theorems of Akopyan, Schwartz and Tabachnikov and of Bialy and Tabachnikov. Using the elliptic curve of the family, we show that the area determines the polygon up to a reflection, find the polygons of largest and smallest area, which proves two conjectures of Cieślak and Mozgawa, and find all points for which the product of the distances to the vertices is constant.

papers.title: Improving X-Ray Baggage Instance Segmentation with Shared Point-Based Mask Refinement
papers.abstract: Overlapping projections and complex object contours make prohibited items difficult to delineate in X-ray baggage images. This study investigates shared point-based mask refinement to improve instance segmentation within Cascade Mask R-CNN. The framework combines a ResNet-101 backbone with an attention-based feature pyramid and progressively updates uncertain mask locations, increasing mask resolution from $28 \times 28$ to $112 \times 112$. A single refinement module is shared across cascade stages and refinement levels, with transformer and multilayer perceptron (MLP) variants used to examine the role of interactions among selected points. Ten configurations were evaluated on the official PIXray split across three training seeds using the original target-instance annotations for evaluation. The transformer and MLP refiners achieved mean mask average precision (AP) of 71.79 and 72.47, respectively, compared with 70.50 for the unrefined detector, yielding gains of 1.29 and 1.97 AP points. The MLP achieved the highest mean mask AP among the evaluated configurations. Both variants also improved boundary agreement on commonly detected objects, supporting improved mask delineation, while detection diagnostics did not establish a corresponding positive gain. These findings demonstrate that shared point-based refinement can improve segmentation quality in the tested cascade architecture using existing target-mask annotations, without additional occluder supervision. Evaluation on independent X-ray datasets is needed to determine how well these improvements generalize.

papers.title: Rounded Potentials Certify Exact Maximum Flow
papers.abstract: The textbook certificate for maximum flow is lopsided: the cut takes one bit per vertex, while the flow takes one number per edge. Indeed, some graphs have $Θ(n^2)$ terminal pairs for which every maximum flow uses $Θ(n^2)$ edges. Yet we show that one short number per vertex suffices for both cut and flow: $n$ vertex potentials, each rounded to $O(\log(nW))$ bits, certify the exact maximum $st$-flow value in any directed graph with integer capacities at most $W$. Exact potentials can have exponentially large representations. Rounding them may violate flow conservation, but the total error across any cut is less than one unit, so integrality of cut capacities absorbs it. Checking conservation is local and linear in the capacities, allowing the same certificate to yield new bounds in four models (capacities are polynomially bounded unless stated otherwise): - Online annotated streaming. $\widetilde{O}(n)$ total cost (help plus space) for the maximum $st$-flow value, optimal up to logarithmic factors, answering a question of Thaler (ICALP 2016) on whether $o(n^2)$ is possible. - Broadcast proof-labeling. $O(\log(n+p))$-bit labels certifying a maximum $st$-flow value of $p$ in directed and undirected graphs with arbitrary capacities, optimal for $p\ge n^{Ω(1)}$, settling that regime of a question of Korman, Kutten, and Peleg (Distributed Computing 2010). - Merlin-Arthur verification. $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ time and $O(n^3\log n)$ proof length for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, improving on previous verification times of $n^{4+o(1)}$ for general capacities and $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ for unit capacities, and answering a question of Akmal (TheoretiCS 2024). - Nondeterministic algorithms. $O(n^{3.614})$ time for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, or $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ if $ω=2$: the first subquartic bound for general edge capacities, answering a question of Trabelsi (SODA 2025).

papers.title: Wideband Terahertz Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS): Bandwidth Limits, Ergodic Rate, and Placement Optimization
papers.abstract: Terahertz (THz) bands offer the vast bandwidth that sixth-generation (6G) networks demand, but their severe path loss makes bringing the radiator close to the user decisive. Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) do exactly this, turning path loss into a programmable parameter by sliding radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, which makes THz their native regime. That regime, however, is inherently wideband and the waveguide is dispersive, whereas every existing PASS analysis is single-frequency and assumes a non-dispersive guide. This paper develops the first wideband, dispersion-aware theory of PASS and uncovers a limitation intrinsic to the pinching mechanism. Because co-phasing by physical position equalizes path length only modulo a wavelength, a pinching array is inherently beam-squint limited, and we show its frequency response is a Dirichlet kernel with a closed-form coherence bandwidth and an irreducible dispersion floor that even true-time-delay (TTD) correction cannot remove. A single unifying law governs the behavior, in which array gain trades against both coherence bandwidth and spatial robustness through one invariant that TTD correction breaks, reaching the floor with far fewer delay elements than a conventional array. We further characterize the wideband ergodic rate under random user locations, show that molecular absorption acts as a deterministic taper that multiplies the squint, and derive a simple rule for the rate-optimal number of pinches. Finally, by exploiting the integer structure of co-phasing, we recast the non-convex placement problem as a mixed-integer program that can be solved exactly in polynomial time. Together, these results move PASS from the narrowband, dispersion-blind setting to the wideband, dispersive regime that THz operation actually requires.

papers.title: Model Immunization Beyond Condition Numbers: The Importance of Plateau Regions
papers.abstract: Harmful fine-tuning can rapidly compromise safety alignment in Large Language Models, underscoring the vulnerability of deployed models to post-release modification. While prior work motivates model immunization by inducing ill-conditioned curvature to slow harmful optimization, this approach is not scalable due to the high computational cost of Hessian estimation. We refine this paradigm by extending the theoretical framework to prioritize plateau regions alongside curvature. We further introduce an immunization algorithm based on efficient Hessian estimation and bounds on the extremal singular values of the Hessian. We demonstrate the proposed immunization framework in three applications: (i) Fine-tuning-as-a-service settings where benign user data may be mixed with poisoned harmful data, (ii) open-weight settings where an adversary can fine-tune on harmful-only data with varied training dynamics, and (iii) robust unlearning, where immunized models better resist relearning attacks after unlearning. Extensive experiments confirm that our approach achieves robust defense against adversarial fine-tuning while largely maintaining general utility and downstream trainability. Our code is available at https://github.com/minhquoc0712/BECON.

papers.title: Online and Fully-Dynamic Sorting
papers.abstract: Online sorting asks how to place $n$ sequentially arriving elements in an array to minimize the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements. Fully-dynamic sorting further extends the problem to allow both element insertions and deletions. Without recourse, these problems face strong lower bounds on the competitive ratio: $Ω(\sqrt{n})$ for online sorting and $Ω(n)$ for fully-dynamic sorting. In sharp contrast, we show that allowing only poly-logarithmic recourse yields at least exponential improvements in the competitive ratio for both problems:(1) Our main algorithmic result is a deterministic fully-dynamic sorting algorithm that is $O(\log^2 n)$-competitive and has $O(\log^4 n)$ amortized recourse per update. We complement this with a lower bound showing that any deterministic algorithm with any $O(\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ competitive ratio has amortized recourse at least $Ω(\sqrt{\log n})$.(2) For the insertion-only setting, we establish a family of approximation--recourse tradeoffs, including $O(\log\log n)$ competitive ratio with $O(\log\log n)$ amortized recourse. Given the lower bound in the fully-dynamic case, this result shows that the insertion-only problem yields exponentially better bounds than the fully-dynamic one.(3) Finally, we show that the stronger approximation-recourse tradeoff for the insertion-only case extends to the fully-dynamic setting when the array has $(1+\varepsilon)n$ space.

papers.title: Isospectral Density Design and Distinct Global Shape Transitions in Weighted Yukawa Droplets
papers.abstract: We study Euclidean perimeter plus Yukawa repulsion with a fixed radial source density and a fixed ordinary volume. For each sufficiently small positive screening parameter, we construct two smooth, positive, strictly increasing densities whose constrained shape Hessians at the unit ball agree for every coupling. Their source masses, Yukawa moments, and ball self-energies also agree. Just above their common first global transition threshold, all minimizers form one rotation orbit of tetrahedral shapes for one density and one orbit of sectoral threefold shapes for the other. Both transitions are continuous, and the minimizing shapes are strictly convex. We obtain the two densities by fixing the boundary data that determine the Hessian and changing the higher derivatives that determine the reduced quartic energy. We compute a positive quartic coefficient, restore the three scalar observables by interior corrections, and add a finite exterior density barrier to control all finite-perimeter competitors.

papers.title: Beyond Semantic Prompts: Unified Watermarking and Access Control for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Text-to-image diffusion services require both traceability of generated content and differentiated access to generation capabilities. However, existing watermarking methods commonly expose watermark control through mechanisms beyond the text-prompt interface, while credential-based access control does not inherently enforce distinct output quality levels. We propose a unified framework that enables customizable multi-bit watermark embedding and tiered access control through a single text prompt. A unified prompt represents watermark messages using designated words and associates protocol structures with different access states. The framework adopts a two-stage training strategy. First, watermark payload partitioning represents messages as designated watermark words, while vocabulary extension assigns each protocol word a dedicated token with a learnable input embedding. Guided by a frozen reference model and a pretrained watermark codec, joint adaptation of the U-Net and protocol-token embeddings transfers message-dependent watermark patterns into the generation process. Second, a prompt-structure recognition network controls feature modulation within the variational autoencoder decoder, which is trained to produce clear watermarked images, blurred previews, or black outputs according to the access state. Experiments demonstrate reliable watermark recovery, robustness to common image-processing operations and evaluated model modifications, and consistent performance across diverse generation settings. The controlled decoder also achieves distinct output behaviors under restricted access while closely preserving reference decoding fidelity and watermark recoverability under full access. Our open-source code and model weights will be public after acceptance.

papers.title: Phase diagram and lattice structure of interlayer vortices in multilayer Ising superconductors in parallel magnetic fields
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate layered $s$-wave Ising superconductors under an in-plane magnetic field using self-consistent solutions of the microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. Comparing bilayer, four-layer, and infinite-layer systems, we determine how the phase diagram and vortex structure evolve with layer number. Compared to standard Ginzburg-Landau treatments, our approach applies over a broader parameter regime and self-consistently resolves the spatial and layer dependence of the gap amplitude without prescribing its form. We find that the field range supporting the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase (defined as having no interlayer vortices) is reduced with increasing layer number and is essentially absent at nonzero magnetic flux in the infinite-layer system, consistent with recent thickness-dependent experiments on multilayer 2H-NbSe$_2$. In the infinite-layer limit, the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase containing interlayer vortices persists to progressively larger in-plane fields as temperature is lowered below the zero-field critical temperature, consistent with the experimentally observed low-temperature enhancement of the upper critical field. The vortex structure also evolves with interlayer hopping: in four-layer systems, for the fluxes and system sizes considered, increasing hopping reorganizes vortices from outer to inner interlayer junctions. At larger hopping, the gap distortion associated with an interior vortex extends to the surface layers, producing gap suppression comparable to that in the interior layers. Representative six-layer calculations show that interior vortices likewise produce a finite, although weaker, modulation of the surface-layer gap. These results highlight layer number and interlayer tunneling as key parameters governing the phase diagram and vortex arrangement in multilayer Ising superconductors.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics
papers.abstract: Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. We compare TabPFN-3.5 with two DeepED baselines, $DeepED_{LSTM}$ and $DeepED_{Transformer}$, on CarbonGlobe's overall evaluation, which trains on a uniform 1/16 sample of sites and tests on the other 50,779, predicting the 40-year state of all seven ED outputs. We then test every model, trained on present-day data only, on ED runs forced by SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 for 2021--2060 in six continental forest regions. With no training, TabPFN-3.5 has the lowest present-day height error of the three models and is within 4% of $DeepED_{LSTM}$ for soil carbon, but is less accurate for AGB, LAI and the carbon fluxes. In 2060, errors are several times larger than at the same sites under present-day forcing, and every model underestimates the biomass that ED gains. Under SSP5-8.5, TabPFN-3.5 is the most accurate model for height, AGB, soil carbon and LAI, with the lowest AGB error in all six regions, although, unlike ED, it predicts no larger biomass gain than under SSP1-2.6. Under SSP1-2.6, no model is best overall.

papers.title: On the Applicability of $p$-adic Numbers in Computational Modules for Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The applicability of $p$-adic arithmetic as an intermediate computational module in an otherwise unchanged machine-learning pipeline is investigated. A one-feature linear regression on the scikit-learn Diabetes dataset serves as the test model. The fitted coefficients are represented in $\mathbb{Q}_p$, predictions are computed in that field, and rational reconstruction is applied to the outputs. In the pyAdic experiments, rational reconstruction either returns no result or produces values that differ from the baseline predictions; changing computational precision can change both the magnitude and sign of the reconstructed value. In SageMath, forward conversions succeed, but the reconstructed predictions differ from the baseline. An alternative representation based on digit reversal fails to preserve ordinary addition because of carry propagation. Under the tested settings, none of the test predictions is reconstructed correctly. These results show that the tested conversion and reconstruction procedures do not provide a compatible intermediate module even for linear regression. Models defined directly over $p$-adic data and operations offer a direction for further investigation.

papers.title: Quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering in nonlocal plasmonics
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering by a fixed collection of smooth, separated metallic particles described by the hard-wall generalized nonlocal optical response (GNOR) model. As the ratio $η$ of the reference screening length to the particle size tends to zero, regularized first-order and second-order transmission conditions approximate the electric far-field operator with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively. The estimates retain retardation and are uniform on compact subplasma frequency intervals with fixed positive damping and for a bounded dimensionless diffusion-to-pressure ratio. The proof combines exact elimination of the longitudinal field, a uniform weak bound for its boundary density, and smoothing by exterior observations. The same error orders hold for fields observed at a fixed positive distance from the particles. We also justify thin-coating representations on bounded tangential wave-number ranges for a planar interface and on fixed finite spherical angular subspaces. For each fixed quasistatic spherical multipole with a simple local pole, the first- and second-order models approximate the pole and its residue with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively.

papers.title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
papers.abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

papers.title: AdaModalX: Synchronization-Free MFM Inference for Distributed Multimodal Mobile Sensing via Progressive Data Orchestration
papers.abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) support generalizable inference in distributed mobile sensing applications by integrating heterogeneous data streams. However, existing MFM inference pipelines typically require complete and synchronized multimodal inputs, whereas mobile sensing streams arrive asynchronously due to network variability and heterogeneous data volumes across modalities. Waiting for all modalities increases end-to-end latency, while inference with incomplete inputs can reduce accuracy. We argue that multimodal inference should depend on the utility of available information rather than modality completeness. Based on this principle, we propose AdaModalX, a progressive multimodal inference framework that decouples inference execution from modality synchronization through runtime utility-aware orchestration. At each device, importance-aware data uploading uses a lightweight probe distilled from the edge-side MFM to allow reliable samples to exit locally while uncertain samples continue uploading. At the edge, on-demand MFM activation constructs candidates from fully received samples and, when needed, imputed features derived from partially received delayed inputs. A lightweight contribution assessor built on frozen MFM encoders estimates candidate utility and activates the MFM once the candidate meets its corresponding utility threshold. Experiments on four mobile sensing applications show that AdaModalX improves the accuracy-latency trade-off, achieving up to 26.97% accuracy improvement and up to 64.75% end-to-end latency reduction.

papers.title: Möbius Invertibility of Rank Invariants
papers.abstract: One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. Möbius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, Möbius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. This work studies the extent to which Möbius inversion can be extended beyond these finiteness conditions. Namely, we formalize the notion of Möbius invertibility, which captures when Möbius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is Möbius invertible. A central result we establish is that Möbius invertibility of the GRI is guaranteed for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules when $d\leq 2$, but may fail when $d>2$. Establishing this failure also corrects an error in the existing literature. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its Möbius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.

papers.title: Optimization Framework for Full-Skyrmionic Polarimetry
papers.abstract: Optical skyrmionic beams hold considerable potential for applications in quantum information and weak-intensity detection. These applications require accurate measurements of full topological observables using imaging Stokes polarimetry, with measurement states optimized in advance to limit the effect of stochastic error sources. However, the optimization framework for general Stokes polarimetries is based on a linear reconstruction chain for Stokes vectors and cannot quantitatively evaluate the nonlinear reconstruction of topological observables. Here, we define full-skyrmionic polarimetry (FSP) and construct its optimization framework from the reconstruction chain for full topological observables. Based on existing polarization evaluating functions (PEF), we introduce topological evaluating functions (TEF) and develop a multi-stage FSP optimization methodology. Numerical results confirm that topological optimization can further improve the reconstruction of topological observables, even when the measurement states are already optimal for polarization. Increasing the redundant projection number also effectively suppresses the effects of all stochastic error sources, providing a low-cost methodology to improve the reconstruction of both polarization and topological observables. The FSP optimization framework can identify topologically optimal configurations for arbitrary FSP structures, providing a guideline for high-precision full-skyrmionic measurements at weak-intensity levels and potential skyrmion ellipsometry.

papers.title: LiveView: Real-Time Camera-Controlled Re-filming of Streaming Videos
papers.abstract: Real-time camera-controlled video re-filming aims to synthesize target views from a streaming source video under online user-specified camera trajectories. This task poses two key challenges: maintaining synchronization and content consistency across views, and achieving low-latency rendering with long-horizon stability. Existing approaches are predominantly designed for offline full-sequence processing and rely on bidirectional attention or costly depth-based geometric preprocessing, making them unsuitable for low-latency streaming scenarios. To address these limitations, we develop a teacher-to-student framework that distills a high-fidelity bidirectional re-filming teacher into a few-step causal autoregressive student. We introduce Cross-Frame Injection to interleave each incoming source frame with its synchronized target latent, thereby establishing direct cross-view correspondence and improving content consistency. To ensure stable long-horizon generation, we further propose Shared Relative RoPE, which bounds temporal indices within the pretrained range, and Cycle Streaming Tuning, which exposes the student to extended cyclic trajectories during streaming training. These designs enable low-latency online video re-filming with precise camera control and sustained spatiotemporal consistency over long streaming rollouts.

papers.title: Stochastic Self-Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotics through imitation learning, yet fine-tuning them with on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is limited. In group-based RL methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), every rollout step requires multi-step ODE integration, and the sampler's limited stochasticity leads to rollout groups with low variance. We propose VLA-SSD, which addresses both high inference latency and limited stochasticity. In particular, our method self-distills a pretrained flow-matching action head into a stochastic one-step policy by conditioning a single-jump generator on a Brownian path. We derive a conditional action density via our stochastic one-step policy, enabling efficient post-training via likelihood-ratio RL algorithms. We show that distilling VLA-SSD from the $π_0$ VLA reduces the action head's forward-pass time by a factor of 7.7, at the cost of a 5.5% relative decrease in the success rate on the LIBERO benchmark. However, by leveraging the increased sample diversity of VLA-SSD during group generation, post-training a $π_{0.5}$ VLA using GRPO yields a 20.6% relative improvement.

papers.title: Designing Deceptive Model Organisms that Successfully Evade Auditing
papers.abstract: AI models can exhibit deceptive behaviors such as strategically underperforming on evaluations (sandbagging), faking alignment, or covertly acting on behalf of a hidden principal. Safe deployment therefore requires auditing techniques that can reliably detect such behaviors. To develop and test these techniques, we can train model organisms (MOs): models that exhibit deceptive behaviors and serve as realistic evaluation testbeds. However, for such testbeds to be informative, MOs must actively anticipate and resist auditing---a gap in prior work that can lead to overestimation of auditing effectiveness and underestimation of safety risks. We address this gap by designing MOs that capture worst-case deceptive behavior and evade high-effort auditing. Focusing on sandbagging, we frame MO design as a security game between an auditor and a deceptive model and identify three design requirements for sandbagging MOs: (i) effectiveness (underperforming on targeted capabilities), (ii) utility preservation (maintaining performance on all other capabilities), and (iii) robustness (resisting auditing). We propose three MOs: two optimized against blackbox auditing techniques and one optimized against both blackbox and whitebox techniques. Through a comprehensive evaluation, we show that, unlike MOs from prior work, our MOs satisfy all three requirements, providing worst-case baselines for developing and evaluating future auditing techniques.

papers.title: VISTA: A Framework for Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming intelligent transportation systems by connecting roadside cameras, edge computing units, vehicles, and traffic infrastructure into a shared sensing and decision-making ecosystem. However, transmitting raw traffic video over vehicle-to-everything (V2X) links is bandwidth-intensive, while deploying large multimodal models directly on resource-constrained vehicles is often impractical. To address these limitations, this article proposes VISTA (Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness), a multimodal vision-language edge-intelligence framework that combines predictive video representation learning with lightweight language-based reasoning to provide communication-efficient traffic situational awareness. In the proposed architecture, roadside surveillance units employ the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA) and an attentive-pooler module to convert traffic video clips into compact future-scene embeddings. These embeddings are transmitted through V2X links to vehicle-mounted systems, where a TinyLlama small language model, enhanced with a custom visual adapter, interprets the embeddings alongside natural-language (NL) traffic queries. VISTA enables vehicles to obtain interpretable traffic information, reason about upcoming scene dynamics, and identify potential collision risks without receiving raw video streams. Experimental results in a digital-twin urban traffic environment show that VISTA achieves 97.77% accuracy and an 89% F1 score for future collision prediction while reducing the communication payload by several orders of magnitude compared with raw RGB video transmission. These results demonstrate the feasibility of embedding-based multimodal intelligence for low-latency, communication-efficient, and safety-oriented IoT-enabled transportation systems.

papers.title: Estimation of jam density and saturation flow at signalized intersections using only low penetration rate connected vehicle GNSS trajectories: Case study using actual data in Tokyo
papers.abstract: The jam density and saturation flow at a signalized intersection are basic inputs to traffic signal management schemes that use connected vehicle (CV) trajectory data. However, methods for estimating the jam density itself from low penetration rate CV trajectories have received little attention. Although a few theoretical methods have been proposed, their application is very limited and it is not clear whether those parameters can be estimated using actual CV data, especially with low penetration rates. This paper analyze such methods, in which the jam density and saturation flow are estimated from long-term historical distribution of low penetration rate CV stop positions accumulated over many signal cycles. The methods are evaluated using actual CV trajectory data collected at three signalized intersections in Tokyo for six months, with a penetration rate on the order of 1--3%. The estimators mostly agree on a jam spacing close to 8~m at the sites at which the queueing pattern is well developed, and the saturation flow estimates lie within roughly 10% of an independent video-based reference at those sites. Furthermore, quantitative criteria for self-evaluation of reliability of the estimates are proposed.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Polynomial Certificates: Universality, Cubic Exactness, and a Weak--Strong Separation
papers.abstract: We study certificates of polynomial nonnegativity based on hyperbolic polynomials and their parameterized Bézoutians and establish three results. First, in the unrestricted hyperzout model of Ng and Saunderson, every nonnegative real form of degree $2r$ in $m$ variables admits a hyperzout representation using an auxiliary hyperbolic form of degree $2r$ in $m+1$ variables with parameters $k=1$ and $μ=r+1$. Second, every homogeneous hyperbolic cubic in five real variables is SOS-hyperbolic in Saunderson's fixed-direction sense: for each hyperbolicity direction $e$, $B_{p,e,v}$ is a matrix SOS for every $v\in\Lam(p,e)$. Third, a general localization proposition turns an interior-SOS central Wronskian and a non-matrix-SOS central Bézoutian into a two-direction weak--strong separation. An icosahedral seed gives a rational example of degree $46$ in $43$ variables for which every $W_{u,v}$ on the cone is an SOS, but some $B_{p,u,v}$ is not a matrix SOS. The obstruction persists at nearby interior directions, giving a rational hyperbolicity direction at which the polynomial is weakly SOS-hyperbolic but not SOS-hyperbolic in Saunderson's fixed-direction sense. The construction is supported by exact rational Gram and trace certificates.

papers.title: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
papers.abstract: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with \texttt{grep}. What does this dense advantage measure? Existing benchmarks cannot tell: they use curated queries, old code and a handicapped BM25. To find out, we build Repo-Premium, a realistic repository-level code-search benchmark. It ranks files in real repositories, with curated and raw queries in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust and Java, pull requests from 2022 to 2026, and a preregistered test pool over $91$ repositories. Our experiments trace the advantage to two sources: evaluation choices that favor dense retrieval, such as splitting files into chunks for BM25 and counting edited tests as relevant, and queries that lack the code's rare identifiers. Expanding the query with LLM-written identifiers (generate-then-grep) helps BM25 far more than dense retrieval, letting it match dense retrieval in every Python pool, even on pull requests opened after the LLM was released. No method we tried predicts which retriever will win on a given query. From these results we derive three guidelines: measure dense gains against a fair lexical baseline, fuse dense retrieval with BM25, and add the code's words to queries that lack them.

papers.title: KVMARK: Fragile Watermarking for KV-Cache Integrity in Latent Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Latent multi-agent communication directly transfers Key-Value (KV) cache tensors between transformer-based agents, bypassing text serialization entirely. While computationally efficient and reasoning accurate, this communication channel is opaque and vulnerable to man-in-the-middle tampering, a threat vector unaddressed by existing text-based or behavioral watermarks, which cannot operate on continuous internal representations. To address this vulnerability, we propose KVMark, a training-free, zero-bit KV-cache watermarking framework to verify inter-agent handoff integrity. Our framework introduces four core technical components: (1) position-dependent sign patterns that guarantee first-order statistical invisibility while preserving downstream attention survival; (2) per-head sign patterns with aligned detection to defeat head-averaging attacks; (3) a three-tier depth-aware strength schedule that equalizes detection sensitivity across transformer layers while maintaining invisibility against nine statistical profiling strategies; and (4) content-bound key derivation that cryptographically binds watermarks to input contexts, preventing replay attacks under Kerckhoffs's principle. Empirical evaluation on a four-agent latent pipeline demonstrates $100\%$ detection across $1{,}500$ handoffs with a $0.0\%$ false positive rate ($\text{AUROC}=1.0$), $100\%$ layer-level tamper localization ($17/17$ attacked layers identified with $0/19$ false positives), and no statistically significant reasoning accuracy degradation across four benchmarks ($N{=}300$--$500$). Furthermore, the framework enables multi-hop cascade verification to isolate compromised agents (500/500 detection at three hops), withstands adaptive white-box adversaries and the Out-of-Sight DiffMean attack (up to $α=8.0$), and generalizes seamlessly to Qwen3-8B without re-tuning (1,500/1,500 TPR).

papers.title: Taint Analysis via Heap-Aware Propagation
papers.abstract: Taint analysis for C depends on how precisely the analysis tracks tainted values as they flow through memory objects. Without field sensitivity, a tainted object field can spuriously taint an entire object, producing significant false alarms. In this paper, we present a field-sensitive taint analysis that combines Data Structure Analysis (DSA) for field-sensitive points-to information with a data-flow analysis for tracking explicit dependencies. We identify that existing DSA-style analyses lose precision on a common object pattern: a C struct object that mixes scalar fields with a flexible array member. When such an array is accessed with symbolic indices, DSA loses points-to field sensitivity for the entire object, inflating false alarms in the data-flow analysis. To address this, we propose I-DSA, which extends DSA by representing field positions as intervals, so that a pointer with symbolic bounds merges only the fields within those bounds. We further develop a sound data-flow analysis based on abstract interpretation. We implement I-DSA on top of SeaDSA and the data-flow analysis inside Crab. Our tool targets LLVM IR and supports configurable taint policies by instrumenting the IR with taint intrinsics. Our experiments show that I-DSA reduces the false alarms caused by this pattern at little cost in the pointer analysis, that SVF, an inclusion-based pointer analysis, shows a similar field-sensitivity loss, and that our taint analysis scales better than PhASAR on real-world programs.

papers.title: XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute
papers.abstract: We present XMimic and XSoma, which learn humanoid motion tracking and locomotion on rough terrain in under a minute of training. Both follow SuperMimic, which learns a world model of the robot and optimizes the policy with analytic gradients through short rollouts imagined in this model. Existing implementations of this method do not make use of larger GPUs, as every training iteration is a long chain of small GPU operations that run one after another. XMimic and XSoma therefore shorten this chain and run the steps of every iteration at the same time on up to four GPUs. We compile the complete training loop with JAX, including the MuJoCo Warp simulator. For locomotion, XSoma leaves only the dynamics of the robot to the world model and computes everything else exactly, including the terrain height under the feet. It learns with a horizon of one second and without a critic. On four H100 GPUs, XMimic learns to track all 40 LAFAN1 clips with the Unitree G1 in 0.86 minutes, 3.7 times faster than BlinkMimic on one GPU. XSoma reaches the tracking target that Holosoma's tests set for FastSAC in 0.77 minutes, 12.3 times faster than FastSAC on one GPU, while needing only an eighth of its environment steps.

papers.title: Generative AI-Driven Parametric Design Optimization Framework for Vehicle Closure Systems
papers.abstract: This study presents a generative AI-driven parametric design optimization framework integrating performance-oriented generation with editable computer-aided design (CAD) and downstream computer-aided engineering (CAE) analysis for industrial vehicle closure systems. The framework is demonstrated on an automotive tailgate assembly with complex geometry, coupled components, and competing performance and feasibility requirements. A production-oriented CATIA model is restructured into a reference-based parametric template with a 13-dimensional design representation. An automated CAD/CAE workflow generates parametric models, performs structural analysis, and constructs a database of mass, maximum displacement, and maximum von Mises stress. Gaussian process regression surrogates predict performance, while diffusion and flow matching models generate design candidates. The design problem minimizes mass and maximum displacement, with stress assessed as an engineering feasibility constraint. Performance-guided generation using surrogate guidance and performance-aware training using a performance-aware loss incorporate engineering objectives, with sensitivity to guidance scale and loss weight evaluated. Generative search is compared with NSGA-II under matched evaluation budgets using a common surrogate model. Selected Pareto-region candidates are reconstructed in CATIA and re-evaluated through native CAE; all verified candidates are successfully regenerated and analyzed. Relative to the baseline, the knee-point design reduces mass by 7.1% and maximum displacement by 29.4%, while extreme verified solutions achieve maximum reductions of 10.3% and 37.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate performance-oriented multi-objective design exploration compatible with editable industrial CAD and native engineering verification.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
papers.abstract: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions. In this study, we propose a physics-informed neural network to efficiently calculate the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators. By incorporating three types of loss functions, we train a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to satisfy the governing PDE for the asymptotic phase and the adjoint equation for the phase gradient. The trained network delivers the phase function accurately and, via automatic differentiation, allows the calculation of the phase gradient governing the oscillator's response to perturbations, which enables rapid entrainment closed-loop control using strong inputs. We validate the approach using three types of limit-cycle oscillators and demonstrate that the PINN can facilitate fast and global phase-locking control.

papers.title: MAGE: Meta-path Adaptive Graph Evidence for Transferable Multimodal Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal graphs integrate textual and visual attributes with relational structures, providing a rich representation of complex real-world data. To enable the broad applicability and reuse of graph models, it is crucial for models trained on source graphs to generalize to unseen graph domains. However, this is challenging because cross-modal interactions among neighbors and the neighboring information needed for prediction can vary across target nodes and graph domains. This gives rise to two key challenges: adaptive cross-modal neighborhood fusion, which captures and integrates cross-modal interactions among neighbors to accommodate variations across nodes and domains; and target-specific evidence selection, which identifies the neighboring textual and visual information needed for each target node to support LLM-based prediction. In light of these challenges, we propose MAGE (Meta-path Adaptive Graph Evidence Prompting), a framework for transferable multimodal graph learning. MAGE represents textual and visual node views separately in a heterogeneous graph and introduces two complementary components. Meta-path Adaptive Multimodal Propagation (MAMP) adaptively aggregates neighborhood information along heterogeneous meta-paths and compresses it into graph-aware soft tokens. Evidence-Guided Instruction Tuning (EGIT) selects relevant neighboring evidence for each query and incorporates its graph-aware representations into instructions for a frozen multimodal LLM. Together, these components support transfer from multiple source graphs to unseen target graphs without target-domain parameter updates. Experiments with three source graphs and four unseen target graphs demonstrate strong cross-domain transfer performance on node classification and link prediction, without requiring parameter updates on the target domains.

papers.title: IntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu
papers.abstract: Multimodal search with image-text queries helps users find notes in user-generated content (UGC) communities and serves as a key search tool for multimodal search agents. For such queries, query-note relevance depends on the user's retrieval intent and cannot be determined by visual or topical similarity alone. Simply reranking visual search results cannot fully address this challenge, as notes relevant to the user's intent may be missing from the initial candidate set. This motivates explicit intent modeling to align candidate retrieval and reranking under consistent relevance criteria. We present IntentFlow, an intent-driven real-time multimodal search system deployed at Xiaohongshu over an index on the order of ten billion entries. IntentFlow represents retrieval objectives with a hierarchical intent taxonomy and uses intent-specific relevance criteria to guide data construction, representation learning, and reranking. An offline agentic data workflow acquires candidates and verifies their relevance under these criteria to produce training supervision. The embedding model combines intent-aware contrastive learning, graded ranking, and distribution distillation, while a compact reranker assesses query-candidate evidence conditioned on predicted hierarchical intents. Evaluations demonstrate that IntentFlow delivers substantial gains in search engagement while supporting real-time search at industrial scale. In a user-level A/B test on the Xiaohongshu platform, IntentFlow outperforms the existing production system based on visual search followed by reranking, achieving relative gains of 28.17% in Top-4 query click-through rate, 18.96% in query click-through rate, and 12.56% in average time spent on search results pages per user. Production monitoring records an end-to-end P50 latency of 1.07 s.

papers.title: The Logic Chain Breaking Point: A Controlled-Variable Benchmark for Reasoning Degradation in Open-Weight Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce The Logic Chain Breaking Point, a controlled-variable benchmark for deductive reasoning in open-weight language models. It spans three phases: (i) pure modus-ponens chain scaling, (ii) distractor resilience with a fixed core chain, and (iii) contradiction detection under primacy versus recency placement. Independent variables follow a powers-of-two sequence $v \in \{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128\}$, with ground truth known by construction. We evaluate sixteen open-weight models across instruction-tuned and reasoning-tuned panels, including a small-model suite and a larger local-model extension. All models are evaluated with greedy decoding under model-appropriate context and output budgets, while context- and length-limited trials are quarantined from the valid accuracy denominator. Our results reveal a sharply non-monotonic difficulty surface: pure deductive chains up to $L=128$ remain near saturation for most models, and distractor noise causes only model-specific degradation at high $D$, while the inconsistent premise condition has the lowest accuracy. Instruction-tuned models, including larger 24B--27B baselines, score essentially zero on inconsistent premise sets, while reasoning-tuned models recover only partially and remain below reliable accuracy. Within this benchmark, inconsistent premise sets are associated with the strongest degradation under the benchmark's abstention-based scoring rule.

papers.title: LEDGE: Separating Critic and Editor Failures in Text-to-Image Self-Correction
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) self-correction combines a vision-language model (VLM) critic that diagnoses errors and proposes instructions with an image editor that executes them. End-to-end evaluation obscures whether failures arise from incorrect diagnoses or an editor unable to execute valid instructions. We introduce LEDGE (Learning Error Diagnosis in Generation and Editing), a framework that separates these bottlenecks. LEDGE compiles oracle edit instructions from GenEval while holding the generated images and the editor fixed, isolating the editor's correction capability from the critic's diagnostic accuracy. On Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, oracle instructions raise GenEval from 72.0% to 81.2%, versus 74.1% for the baseline VLM critic. Yet 435 of 644 failed images remain unrepaired, exposing a substantial editor gap. We also use oracle labels from disjoint training prompts to supervise the critic. Oracle supervision raises exact diagnosis from 33.3% (the same VLM with our structured output, untrained) to 70.8%. With the same editor, the resulting critic improves GenEval from 42.2% (uncorrected) to 59.4% on Stable Diffusion 1.5, against 50.9% for the baseline critic, and from 72.0% to 76.0% on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, despite training only on Stable Diffusion 1.5. Improvements transfer to unseen object classes, a second editor, and independent T2I-CompBench judges and prompts. A small human evaluation confirms the ranking in estimated net corrections but suggests a smaller gain than detector-based evaluation. LEDGE thus distinguishes two limits of self-correction: knowing what to fix and being able to fix it.

papers.title: Explainable Federated Learning via Global-Local Attribution Alignment
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables on-device training without centralizing data, yet existing systems still struggle to provide explanations that are both locally faithful and globally consistent under strict privacy and bandwidth constraints. Prior approaches either keep explanations siloed across clients, transmit heavy or sensitive artifacts, or replace expressive task models with interpretable surrogates that sacrifice accuracy. We propose xFedAlign, a model-agnostic framework that decouples task optimization in parameter space from explanation coordination in a compact group space. Each client distills a lightweight surrogate to produce private, per-class top-k attribution artifacts, which are robustly aggregated by the server into a Global Explanation Prior that softly aligns client explanations without constraining task learning. Across image, text, and tabular benchmarks with IID and non-IID partitions, xFedAlign matches FedAvg accuracy while consistently reducing explanation drift and improving deletion and insertion AUC relative to Local-XAI, FedAttr-Agg, and Fed-XAI, with only a few kilobytes of additional communication per round. Privacy and robustness evaluations further demonstrate reduced membership inference advantage and increased resistance to attribution poisoning, enabling consistent and trustworthy explanations in federated learning.

papers.title: Spectral Instability of Wasserstein Entropy on Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact homogeneous Riemannian manifold, and let $m$ be its invariant probability measure. At $m$, the Wasserstein entropy Hessian has a sharp lower bound given by $λ_1$, the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $M$.
